Headline: Chris Rodriguez rushed four times for five yards in the Jaguars’ Week 10 win over the Titans.
News Snippet: Rodriguez spent most of the day watching Bhayshul Tuten rack up a career-high 29 touches, 26 of which were carries. Tuten also saw all the goal line work and eventually found the end zone late in the fourth quarter. With Tuten’s role on the rise, fantasy managers can likely cut ties with Rodriguez ahead of Week 11. He will be buried in the RB4 ranks when the Jags take on the Giants.

Headline: Isaiah Williams caught 4-of-7 targets for 24 yards in the Jets’ Week 10 loss to the Bills.
News Snippet: Williams stepped into a bigger role with Omar Cooper Jr. (ankle) leaving this game after the Jets’ first offensive play. The 25-year-old could have had a bigger day, but a long catch-and-run was called back due to offsetting penalties. If Cooper Jr. were to miss Week 11, Williams could be a deep league FLEX option against the Chargers, but he’s likely not in for a huge role.

Headline: Xavier Hutchinson caught 4-of-9 targets for 58 yards and a touchdown in Houston’s Week 10 loss to the Browns.
News Snippet: His touchdown catch came on a misdirection play where he camped out and waited for the Browns to react to the initial action before getting a wide-open path to the end zone. After Tank Dell returned and the Texans traded for Marvin Harrison Jr., there remained Hutchinson, now with three touchdowns in three games after the bye. He’ll be a reasonable FLEX play against the Colts this week with six teams on bye.

Headline: Parker Washington caught 7-of-9 targets for 152 yards and a touchdown in the Jaguars’ Week 10 win over the Titans.
News Snippet: Washington was unstoppable in the first half with three gains of 30 or more yards plus a short touchdown. He entered halftime with six grabs for 148 yards. The fact that he was on pace for nearly 300 yards and finished with “only” 152 is a slightly disappointing outcome, but there wasn’t much of a reason for the Jags to keep airing it out in the second half. The Titans weren’t putting up much of a fight on offense and the Jags leaned on their ground game, preventing Washington from having a truly insane day. Fantasy managers will have to live with their 28.2 PPR points. Washington is pushing for a WR1 ranking as he heads into a Week 11 matchup with the Giants.

Headline: Adonai Mitchell caught 3-of-8 targets for 59 yards in the Jets’ Week 10 loss to the Bills.
News Snippet: One of the incomplete passes was one that hit Mitchell in the hands, and he had two feet in bounds, but he let go of the ball to readjust his grip and was unable to remain in bounds, wiping out a 15-yard gain. With Omar Cooper Jr. leaving this game with an ankle injury, Mitchell could have a more dependable role next week against the Chargers, which would put him on the FLEX radar.

Headline: Nico Collins caught 9-of-16 targets for 94 yards and a touchdown in Houston’s Week 10 win over the Browns.
News Snippet: Despite the fun line, it wasn’t exactly a game that left you feeling great about Collins. He looked heavily fatigued at times, notably grabbing his shoulder after one sideline collision, and also managed to cut short a route that led to C.J. Stroud’s only interception and cost the Texans at least three points at the end of the first half. Assuming he’s healthy, he’ll be in the WR1 mix again next week against the Colts on Thursday night.

Headline: Garrett Wilson caught 7-of-14 targets for 106 yards in the Jets’ Week 10 loss to the Bills.
News Snippet: No other Jets player had more than seven targets, so Wilson was the clear focus of the passing attack. That continued when Cade Klubnik came into the game as well. Wilson made a few tough catches and was targeted twice in the end zone as well. Unfortunately, the wide receiver was also charged with a fumble on a botched hook-and-ladder play where he was hit as he was attempting the pitch, which went astray and was recovered by the Bills. Wilson remains the clear top option in this passing attack and could still be a low-end WR2 with Klubnik under center next week against the Chargers.

Headline: Emari Demercado rushed seven times for 16 yards in Houston’s Week 10 loss to the Browns.
News Snippet: 13 of those yards came on one carry. Demercado saw the bulk of the opportunities with Woody Marks (concussion) sidelined in the third quarter. Both Demercado’s history and the broader history of Texans running backs over the past several years would tell you there’s little fantasy value in him next week assuming that he becomes their main ballcarrier. Nevertheless, with six teams on bye, he’ll be a reasonable FLEX play against the Colts if David Montgomery remains sidelined.

Headline: Jonathan Taylor rushed 16 times for 83 yards in the Colts’ Week 10 win over the Dolphins, adding 2 receptions for 20 yards.
News Snippet: Taylor totaled 103 yards from scrimmage against the Dolphins, officially eclipsing 10,000 scrimmage yards for his career. Despite staying with the team after the trade deadline, Taylor still ceded many backfield opportunities to Seth McGowan. He saw 23 more snaps but just four more carries while McGowan scored a red zone touchdown. Taylor fumbled in the second quarter; it would have been the 27-year-old’s fifth lost fumble of the season if the Colts did not recover. He was also stuffed at the one-yard line on a second quarter goal-line carry. Taylor still sees an elite workload, but the Colts offense does not generate many scoring opportunities and McGowan is cutting into red zone work. Facing the Texans in Week 11, Taylor is still a fantasy RB1, though he does not carry the same top-five ceiling that managers drafted him for.

Headline: Braelon Allen rushed eight times for 40 yards in the Jets’ Week 10 loss to the Bills.
News Snippet: Allen looked pretty good as a runner but didn’t get a lot of opportunities with the Jets trailing most of the game. Allen played eight fewer snaps than Breece Hall, took three fewer carries, and ran a route on four fewer dropbacks, but he didn’t command nearly as many targets. It’s hard to trust Allen in fantasy next week against the Chargers.

Headline: Trevor Lawrence completed 25-of-35 passes for 352 yards, three touchdowns, and one interception in the Jaguars’ 40-23, Week 10 win over the Titans.
News Snippet: Lawrence added 27 yards with his legs. He picked apart the Titans’ defense in the first half, finding big completion after big completion via Parker Washington. With the Titans failing to do that much on offense, things slowed down in the second half, but two of Lawrence’s touchdowns did come after the break. The interception was the result of a batted pass that popped up and into the hands of Titans linebacker Cedric Gray. Lawrence’s 352 yards are his highest total since Week 5 of the 2024 season. Playing nearly MVP-caliber football, Lawrence will be a top-half QB1 for his Week 11 game against the Giants.

Headline: Breece Hall rushed 11 times for 40 yards in the Jets’ Week 10 loss to the Bills, adding 67 yards receiving on four catches.
News Snippet: Hall wasn’t able to get much going on the ground against the Bills, but he did look good as a receiver. Hall played eight more snaps than Braelon Allen, including running a route on 19 dropbacks to 16 for Allen, but the timeshare on a bad offense is going to limit both of their fantasy upside. Hall is more of a high-end FLEX option or RB3 next week against the Chargers.

Headline: C.J. Stroud completed 20-of-38 passes for 211 yards, three touchdowns and an interception in Houston’s 27-24, Week 10 loss to the Browns.
News Snippet: What had started off as a fun 17-0 lead melted away into a dispiriting, likely season-ending loss to the Browns to fall to 3-6. Stroud managed to go just 5-of-19 for 21 yards in the second half as his receivers were blanketed in man coverage and their run game, as usual, was dead on arrival. Especially after Woody Marks left with a concussion. Stroud will probably retain low-end QB1 value against what looks to be a dire Colts defense in Week 11.

Headline: Josh Downs caught 4-of-5 targets for 53 yards and a touchdown in the Chiefs’ Week 10 win over the Falcons.
News Snippet: Playing sporadic snaps for most of the first half, the Chiefs finally cut Downs loose on their final drive of the second quarter and were rewarded with an 18-yard score where Downs cooked Billy Bowman in coverage. He then proceeded to see only one look after halftime, but Downs’ presence sure seemed to be creating more space for all involved. Not that Downs is that good, but that the presence of any legitimate wideout was all that was needed to get this attack operating on a higher level again. With his involvement certain to ramp up quickly, Downs can be considered a solid WR3 for Week 11 against Arizona.

Position: Concepcion caught 3-of-8 passes for 21 yards in Cleveland’s Week 10 win over the Texans, adding a six-yard touchdown rush on his only carry.
Headline: KC Concepcion caught 3-of-8 passes for 21 yards in Cleveland’s Week 10 win over the Texans, adding a six-yard touchdown rush on his only carry.
News Snippet: He dropped a perfectly-placed deep ball in the first quarter and was seen riding an exercise bike on the sideline afterwards, but he got off the bench and scored on a misdirection touchdown play in the third quarter. With a 129-yard game and two touchdowns mixed among his last four games, Concepcion should likely remain in the WR3 mix as we hit his bye week.

Headline: Dalton Kincaid caught 2-of-3 passes for 58 yards in the Bills’ Week 10 win over the Jets.
News Snippet: Kincaid had one huge play in the third quarter, with a 54-yard catch down the sideline. There wasn’t much else to his day, but he was targeted in the end zone on a play that wound up being called defensive pass interference. He remains more of a high-end TE2 in a crowded passing attack in Buffalo.

Headline: Jalen Coker did not catch any of his four targets in the Panthers’ Week 10 win against the Saints.
News Snippet: Coker had one rush for three yards but was otherwise invisible. The usually pass-first Panthers went mega run-heavy against the Saints, limiting targets for every Carolina pass catcher. Coker, who ran a route on 33 of 36 Panthers drop backs, was seen yelling in frustration on the sideline in the second half. Coker has done almost nothing since his Week 1 explosion against the Bears. He has four or fewer receptions in five games this season. Coker will be a deep league flex in Week 11 against Baltimore.

Headline: Daniel Jones completed 11-of-22 passes for 108 yards, one touchdown, and two interceptions in the Colts’ 24-22, Week 10 win over the Dolphins, adding five carries for nine yards.
News Snippet: With a pass-catching group depleted after the trade deadline, the Colts offense did just enough to beat the Dolphins. Jones was nearly intercepted on the first pass of the game while he fumbled out of bounds on the Colts’ second possession. He threw a fourth-down interception in the second quarter, but recovered with a touchdown pass to Laquon Treadwell towards the end of the first half. The Colts offense faltered yet again in the second half, with Jones throwing a pick-six in the third quarter and failing to connect with pass-catchers downfield. Colts fans booed the offense off the field nearly every fourth quarter possession. The Colts defense was responsible for one of the team’s touchdowns, with the offense only posting a field goal in the second half. Jones is not a quarterback that needs to be rostered for fantasy purposes; he should only be a desperation play for Superflex leagues for Week 11 against the Texans.

Headline: Denzel Boston caught 1-of-2 targets for 16 yards in Cleveland’s Week 10 win over the Texans.
News Snippet: He did manage some good punt returns, but the Browns weren’t able to get their deep-ball offense going and mostly let Derek Stingley take Boston out of the game. Boston isn’t necessarily a must-hold through shallow leagues at the bye, as he’s been held under 50 yards in five of his last six games, but the target count has been stronger than this dud generally, and he was likely playing hurt here.

Headline: Chuba Hubbard had 27 rushes for 92 yards and two touchdowns in the Panthers’ Week 10 win against the Saints, adding five catches for 72 yards.
News Snippet: The entire Carolina offense revolved around Hubbard in this one, as the Panthers ditched their pass-heavy approach for an ultra run-heavy offense against a middle New Orleans defense. Hubbard had a couple long plays and a touchdown called back on penalties too. He plodded along for much of the game before exploding for a long gain on a well-designed screen play late in the fourth quarter. Hubbard, who now has seven games with at least 17 rushes, has been one of the most reliable running backs in fantasy this season. That might change a bit when Jonathon Brooks returns from injury, perhaps in Week 11 against the Ravens.

Headline: Jerry Jeudy caught 2-of-4 targets for 74 yards in Cleveland’s Week 10 win over the Texans.
News Snippet: He had a 65-yard field-flipper to get Cleveland their first score of the game. That was about the only deep pass the Browns connected on, but it got them going. Jeudy’s been a reasonable third wideout for the Browns this year but nobody you should consider keeping on fantasy rosters through a bye unless you’re in a very, very deep league.

Headline: Keon Coleman caught 1-of-3 passes for 11 yards in the Bills’ Week 10 win over the Jets.
News Snippet: Coleman did make an impressive second catch in traffic, but the play was called back due to an illegal shift penalty. He also took a hit to his helmet on the same play and had to go into the blue medical tent. He was eventually cleared and returned to play, but it’s a situation to watch at practice this week.

Headline: Khalil Shakir caught 2-of-3 targets for 26 yards receiving in the Bills’ Week 10 win over the Jets.
News Snippet: Shakir also added 29 yards rushing on three carries, but two of those were simply screens thrown backwards, so they counted as runs. When you factor that in, Shakir had five targets in this one, which was the second-most of any receiver on the Bills. He remains a safe floor option because of his consistent role in the offense, but there isn’t a big fantasy ceiling here unless he breaks multiple tackles after a short completion.

Headline: Kyle McCord completed 17-of-32 passes for 209 yards and a fumble in the Dolphins’ 24-22, Week 10 loss to the Colts, adding two carries for four yards and a touchdown.
News Snippet: Making his first career start in his NFL debut, McCord had a mix of explosive plays and turnover-worthy plays while taking three sacks on the day. The Dolphins offense committed a false start on the first snap and McCord briefly had his throwing hand looked at after hitting it on a helmet on the Dolphins’ first possession. He missed Greg Dulcich on a fourth down in the red zone in the first half and fumbled for a Colts touchdown to open the second half. McCord was able to hit more explosive plays in the fourth quarter with the Colts’ top two cornerbacks out with injury. He rushed for a touchdown to open the fourth quarter and get the Dolphins within two points. The Dolphins could not finish the comeback, mainly due to kicking woes. McCord showed the desire to put the ball in danger to hunt explosive plays in the second half, a good sign that he can keep a player like Caleb Douglas fantasy-relevant. With six teams on bye, McCord can be considered a QB2 against the Bills for Week 11.

Headline: Bhayshul Tuten rushed 26 times for 88 yards and a touchdown in the Jaguars’ Week 10 win over the Titans, adding three catches for 25 yards.
News Snippet: Tuten spent most of Sunday running into crowded boxes and churning out low-wattage gains. He was also stuffed at the goal line twice. Both were on different drives. Fantasy managers were finally rewarded for their persistence with a six-yard stroll into the end zone inside the two-minute warning. Tuten easily set a new career-high in carries while Chris Rodriguez was limited to a measly four attempts. After seeing 29 touches today, Tuten will continue to push for an RB1 ranking when he takes on the Giants next week.

Headline: Dylan Sampson rushed four times for six yards in Cleveland’s Week 10 win over the Texans, adding four catches for 31 yards on six targets.
News Snippet: Sampson outsnapped Quinshon Judkins 35-32 as the Browns had to dig their way out of a 17-0 hole against the Texans defense. Since returning from injured reserve Sampson has generated 12 catches for 121 yards through the air, not unusable numbers even if they’re not exactly a PPR scam. Sampson can be dropped in shallower leagues during Cleveland’s Week 11 bye.

Headline: DJ Moore caught 4-of-6 targets for 90 yards and a touchdown in the Bills’ Week 10 win over the Jets.
News Snippet: Bills saw twice as many targets as the next most-targeted player on the Bills, and connected with Josh Allen on a deep 45-yard touchdown pass in the third quarter. When he’s been healthy, Moore has been a really solid weapon in this Buffalo offense, and should be a high-end WR2 next week against the Dolphins.

Headline: Emmett Johnson rushed 22 times for 101 yards in the Chiefs’ Week 10 win over the Falcons, adding six receptions for 70 yards and two touchdowns.
News Snippet: Making a spot start in place of Kenneth Walker III (groin), fifth-round rookie Johnson was electric from the opening whistle, routinely tacking on extra yardage by either dragging tacklers or simply juking them out of their cleats. Johnson almost never took a negative play, and was so, so slippery in the open field or with any steam whatsoever. He was the Chiefs’ No. 2 receiver with 6/70/2, and actually the most targeted with seven looks. It was the kind of all-around performance we knew was possible from Johnson’s pre-draft profile but that we just have not seen because of Walker’s dominance. With Walker truly questionable for Week 11 against the Cardinals until we hear otherwise, Johnson would be an RB1 if given another start against the lowly Birds. Even if Walker goes, Johnson’s FLEX standing is now on much firmer ground.

Headline: James Cook rushed 18 times for 157 yards and a touchdown in the Bills’ Week 10 win over the Jets.
News Snippet: The Bills leaned on Cook heavily in this one, not showing much of a belief that the Jets were going to pile up many points on offense. It was a solid day overall for Cook, but he then ripped off a career-high 74-yard touchdown run in the fourth quarter that not only sealed the win for the Bills but also made it a big fantasy day for Cook. The 27-year-old could have had an even bigger day, but he dropped what likely would have been a 15-yard touchdown catch. Cook should be a rock-solid RB1 next week against the Dolphins as well.

Headline: Patrick Mahomes completed 22-of-35 passes for 348 yards and five touchdowns in the Chiefs’ 35-13, Week 10 win over the Falcons.
News Snippet: Breaking Josh Downs into the Chiefs’ undermanned receiver corps, Mahomes ended up having his first five-score passing effort since Week 1 of the 2022 season. Heavens to Betsy. The 348 yards were also his fourth most since that MVP campaign for years ago. All this when the only addition was Josh Downs. Of course, it helped that Mahomes was facing a downtrodden, disinterested Falcons side, but it really did seem like the presence of another legitimate wideout was creating more space for everybody. That even included Rashee Rice, who caught a legitimate down-field bomb, and Andrew Armstrong, who housed a late 43-yard score where Mahomes just kind of chucked it up. Two of Mahomes’ touchdowns went to spot-starting running back Emmett Johnson, who was electric in the open field. This had the feel of a sort of deliverance for the Kansas City side, and it should continue in Week 11 against the Cardinals. The schedule stiffens after that, if not really the opposing defenses. Mahomes is back to every-week QB1 status, and should frequently be a high-end option.

Headline: Quinshon Judkins rushed 10 times for 38 yards and a touchdown in Cleveland’s Week 10 win over the Texans.
News Snippet: He added three catches for 33 yards on five targets as part of a robust screen game. Judkins has continued to see reasonable usage on the ground for a team that runs plenty, but he has yet to crack 100 yards in a game and this was just his fourth touchdown of the season. He actually was outsnapped by Dylan Sampson today, though it’s clear that happened because the Browns fell behind 17-0 before making their comeback. He’ll head into the bye as a borderline RB2.

Headline: Bryce Young completed 17-of-30 attempts for 200 yards in the Panthers’ Week 10 win against the Saints, adding one rush for one yard.
News Snippet: It was one of Young’s worst performances of the season considering the middle competition. Young posted a negative EPA per drop back and was 10 percent under his expected completion rate against New Orleans. His statistical day would have been a little less bleak if Darren Waller had been able to hang on to what would have been a 30-yard score in the first half. Young, who regular missed open wideouts in the intermediate areas, has struggled for most of the past month. Young will be a superflex option in Week 11 against the Ravens.

Headline: Deshaun Watson completed 25-of-40 passes for 312 yards and an interception in Cleveland’s 27-24, Week 10 win over the Texans, adding eight carries for 49 yards and a touchdown.
News Snippet: Watson and the Browns used Houston’s aggressiveness against them, managing 65 passing yards on 13 passes behind the line of scrimmage. His best throw was a strike to Harold Fannin Jr. on Cleveland’s final drive of the game, a 30-yarder that moved the Browns into a goal-to-go situation they would quickly convert. Watson has returned stable QB2 superflex value at a bottom of the basement price this year. He’ll head into the Week 11 bye looking like a reasonable bet to continue doing that.

Headline: Jordyon Tyson caught 7-of-13 targets for 80 yards in the Saints’ Week 10 loss to the Panthers.
News Snippet: The Saints ramped up Tyson’s snaps and routes in his second game of the season, as the rookie ran a route on 32 of the team’s 47 drop backs on the day and easily led all New Orleans pass catchers in targets and receiving yards. Chris Olave, meanwhile, was limited to three catches for 30 yards on five targets. Tyson was targeted both in the short and intermediate areas, and nearly came up with a couple downfield grabs on poorly-thrown balls from Tyler Shough. The Saints saw fit to target Tyson twice on backfield screen looks in the second half. That kind of usage suggests Tyson could be an outsized part of the Saints offense going forward. He’ll be a WR3 option in Week 11 against the Bears.

Headline: Cade Klubnik completed 11-of-20 passes for 137 yards and an interception in the Jets’ 31-12, Week 10 loss to the Bills.
News Snippet: Klubik also added 26 yards rushing on the day. The rookie from Clemson looked pretty good for most of the second half, with no problem driving the ball down the field to his receivers. Some of those passes sailed on him, and he held onto the ball too long at times, but he has the arm and the ability to make enough throws to move the ball down the field and keep the Jets’ receivers relevant for fantasy football. He may have to start next week against the Chargers with Geno Smith (head/ankle) leaving this game early.

Headline: Josh Allen completed 11-of-21 passes for 196 yards with one touchdown and one interception in the Bills’ 31-12, Week 10 win over the Jets, adding two rushing touchdowns on the ground.
News Snippet: The Bills leaned heavily on James Cook in this one, with Allen dropping back to pass just 21 times. When the Bills did pass, they took a few big shots down the field, which resulted in a long touchdown pass to D.J. Moore, but also a long interception on third down in what was ultimately an “arm punt.” Of Allen’s two rushing touchdowns, only one of them was on a tush push. The Bills quarterback has now rushed for 10+ touchdowns in four straight seasons, tying Jalen Hurts (2021-24) for the longest streak by a quarterback in NFL history, and he has 324 total touchdowns in his career, which is now the most by any player in their first 10 seasons in NFL history. He will look for another big fantasy day in Week 11 against the Dolphins.

Headline: Christian Benford has been ruled out for the remainder of Week 10 with a groin injury.
News Snippet: Benford was questionable to play in Week 10 with a wrist injury but was cleared to go. He then injured his groin in the fourth quarter and will not return to the game. The Bills are set to face the Dolphins in Week 11 before facing the Chiefs the following week, so there is a chance that they hold their top cornerback out for next week. We’ll have to see if he is able to practice at all during the week.

Headline: Dorian Williams is questionable to return in Week 10 against the Jets due to a calf injury.
News Snippet: Williams was hurt at the beginning of the fourth quarter and was taken to the blue medical tent. The Bills are up 24-12 with under eight minutes to go, so they may hold Williams out even if he is cleared to return.

Headline: Dee Alford was ruled out of Week 10 against the Jets with a concussion.
News Snippet: Alford was first evaluated for a concussion after he was hit by tight end Mason Taylor on an illegal pick play. He was cleared to return, but then, in the second quarter, he made a nice pass break-up and almost secured a one-handed interception, but his head slammed into the turf. His status for Week 11 against the Dolphins will be up in the air.

Headline: Sauce Gardner (calf) is questionable to return in Week 10 against the Dolphins.
News Snippet: Gardner exited the game with a leg injury in the third quarter. He headed to the locker room and the Colts listed him as questionable to return. Gardner had dealt with a calf injury earlier this season, so it is possible he is dealing with a re-aggravation of the same injury.

Headline: Geno Smith went to the locker room with an ankle injury during Week 10 against the Bills.
News Snippet: Smith was evaluated for a concussion during halftime but cleared to return. On his first drive back in the third quarter, he took another big hit from safety Cole Bishop and limped off the field into the blue medical tent. He then went into the locker room, which will leave Cade Klubnik as the Jets’ only healthy quarterback on the roster. If Smith is done for the day, he will have completed 12-for-21 passes for 148 yards during his two quarters of play. The Jets will hope he can return next week against the Chargers.

Headline: Eli Raridon caught his only target for six yards in the Patriots’ Week 10 loss to the Lions.
News Snippet: Coming off a six-target game in Week 9, Raridon’s role all but evaporated today. He could pop up for another TE2 week down the line, but fantasy managers don’t need to hold him through the Pats’ Week 11 bye.

Headline: Hunter Henry caught 2-of-3 targets for 22 yards in the Patriots’ Week 10 loss to the Lions.
News Snippet: Henry couldn’t get anything going while catching passes from Tommy DeVito for the better part of four quarters. DeVito averaged 3.4 yards per attempt on 24 throws in the blowout loss. Henry would tumble down the TE2 ranks if DeVito starts the Pats’ next game. With a bye week on tap, the hope will be that Drake Maye is available when New England takes on the Chargers in Week 12.

Headline: Raiders declared WR Dont’e Thornton Jr., Malik Benson, S Tristin McCollum, S Dalton Johnson, G Bryce Cabeldue and DT Thomas Booker IV inactive for Week 10 against the Seahawks.
News Snippet: Tre Tucker and Brock Bowers will function as the only viable pass catchers for Fernando Mendoza in his first NFL start against a tough Seattle defense. The Raiders will be without two key safeties, making the matchup slightly better for Drew Lock and his pass catchers.

Headline: Seahawks declared RB Emanuel Wilson, QB Sam Darnold, CB Avery Smith, LG Quenton Nelson, LT Charles Cross, NT Deven Eastern, and DT Leonard Williams inactive for Week 10 against the Raiders.
News Snippet: Wilson will be a healthy scratch once again now that Zach Charbonnet is healthy. Both Charbonnet and Jadarian Price profile as legit fantasy plays against a Raiders rush defense that has been the worst in the league by most metrics over the past six weeks. Look for the Seahawks to be particularly run heavy with Drew Lock banged up.

Headline: Charvarius Ward (shin) is questionable to return in Week 10 against the Dolphins.
News Snippet: Ward went down with a leg injury after a couple of pass-breakups in the third quarter. He limped to sideline and was later carted to the locker room. The Colts declared Ward questionable to return.

Headline: Geno Smith cleared concussion protocol and returned to Week 10 against the Bills.
News Snippet: Smith took a big hit on the Jets’ last play of the first half and was evaluated for a concussion at halftime. Rookie Cade Klubnik played the first drive and led the Jets on a 61-yard drive that ended in a field goal. However, with Smith cleared to return, Klubnik will head back to the bench.

Headline: Demario Douglas caught 1-of-3 targets for four yards in the Patriots’ Week 10 loss to the Lions.
News Snippet: Douglas finished third among the team’s wideouts in targets behind A.J. Brown and Mack Hollins. Brown left the game with a hamstring injury in the fourth quarter and did not return. His absence could open up more work for Douglas, but the Pats are on bye after their trip to Germany. Fantasy managers don’t need to hold Douglas through their week off.

Headline: Woody Marks (concussion evaluation) left Houston’s Week 10 game against the Browns and was ruled out.
News Snippet: He was sandwiched between a pair of defenders on a third-quarter run and eventually walked off between trainers. Marks had 65 total yards before leaving, including one catch for 15 yards. With the short week ahead of them, the Texans will likely not have Marks available on Thursday night, leaving fantasy managers ignoring Emari Demercado and Dare Obungowale unless David Montgomery can play.

Headline: Myles Garrett (knee) is active for Week 10 against the Cardinals.
News Snippet: Garrett and Aaron Donald should have productive outings against a Cardinals offensive line that will be playing with a third-string left tackle and a backup center. Rookie QB Carson Beck will also be making his first career start. The Rams D/ST unit should put up points today.

Headline: Trent McDuffie (back) is active for Week 10 against the Cardinals.
News Snippet: McDuffie sat out in Week 9 after injuring his back in Week 8. He missed Weeks 6-7 with a groin injury. Getting him back in the lineup provides the Rams’ secondary with a serious boost. He should play very well against a Cardinals wide receiver corps made up of backups. Myles Garrett (knee) and S Kam Curl (toe) are also active. The Rams declared QB Ty Simpson, S Maximus Pulley, LS Joe Cardona, OLB Darryl Peterson, OL Steve Avila, OL Keagen Trost and OLB Desjuan Johnson. Simpson will serve as the emergency third quarterback.

Headline: Trent Williams (shoulder) is active for the 49ers’ Week 10 game against the Cowboys.
News Snippet: Williams is active despite only logging one limited practice this week. The future Hall of Famer will man his normal spot at bookend left tackle against the Cowboys. Linebacker Dre Greenlaw is also active, giving the Niners two of their key starters in this one. The 49ers have declared QB Kurtis Rourke, WR Mike Evans, OL Enrique Cruz Jr., LB Tatum Bethune, and WR Brandin Cooks inactive for Week 10.

Headline: Mack Hollins caught 5-of-6 targets for 48 yards in the Patriots’ Week 10 loss to the Lions.
News Snippet: A.J. Brown left this game late with a hamstring injury but was struggling before getting banged up. With the WR1 doing nothing, Hollins stepped up with team-highs in catches and yards. He was, however, catching passes from Tommy DeVito, who took over for an injured Drake Maye. Hollins could see more work if Romeo Doubs remains on IR and Brown is out once again, but we won’t know much about either player until after the Pats’ upcoming bye week.

Headline: Dylan Parham is questionable to return to Week 10 against the Bills with a knee injury.
News Snippet: The Jets’ starting left guard went down with a knee injury in the second quarter. The injury didn’t look good, but he was able to walk off the field and into the blue tent on his own. We’ll see what further testing reveals, but he’s been one of the Jets’ best linemen.

Headline: Travis Kelce (ankle, questionable) returned for the second quarter of Kansas City’s Week 10 game against the Falcons.
News Snippet: Kelce ended up missing about a quarter of action. He figures to be on a snap count for the rest of the afternoon, but we would have to imagine he will be a point of targets emphasis when he is on the field.

Headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Aidan Hutchinson (knee) is expected to be out “for the foreseeable future.”
News Snippet: Hutchinson injured his knee while celebrating a sack in the first quarter of Detroit’s Week 10 win over the Patriots. He jumped into the air and his right knee buckled as he landed. He will undergo more testing, but it looks like the Lions will be without their top pass-rusher for a while. Hutchinson has six sacks in nine games this year.

Headline: Bernhard Raimann (concussion) was ruled out of Week 10 against the Dolphins.
News Snippet: Raimann headed to the locker room to be evaluated for a concussion in the first half of the Colts’ Week 10 game agains the Dolphins. The Colts promptly ruled him out for the game later in the second quarter. Luke Tenuta comes in at left tackle for Raimann.

Headline: Isaac TeSlaa caught 2-of-5 targets for 19 yards and a touchdown in the Lions’ Week 10 win over the Patriots.
News Snippet: TeSlaa beat his man off the line of scrimmage for a 12-yard score early in the second quarter. He was surprisingly involved in this contest, logging just his third game with more than three targets on the year. TeSlaa hadn’t seen more than two targets in a game since Week 4. We don’t expect this to be the new norm, so fantasy managers shouldn’t chase this performance on waivers.

Headline: Sione Vaki rushed six times for 28 yards in the Lions’ Week 10 win over the Patriots.
News Snippet: Vaki operated as the RB2 once again. Three of his carries came on the Lions’ penultimate drive, though Jared Goff was still on the field. Dan Campbell pulled his starters for the team’s final possession and Jacob Saylors closed out the game. Vaki is the backup fantasy managers should roster as Jahmyr Gibbs insurance, but he doesn’t hold any standalone fantasy value.

Headline: Jameson Williams caught 4-of-7 targets for 50 yards in the Lions’ Week 10 win over the Patriots.
News Snippet: Williams didn’t post an elite box score, but he did earn his highest target total since Week 7. The speedster earned a healthy 22 percent target share and finished second on the team in receptions, tied with Amon-Ra St. Brown. Williams has generally been a boom/bust wideout, but he has at least 40 yards in all but two games this year. He’ll remain at the top of the WR3 ranks when he takes on the Bucs next week.

Headline: Omar Cooper Jr. is questionable to return in Week 10 against the Bills due to an ankle injury.
News Snippet: On the Jets’ first play of the game, Cooper Jr. was blocking for Breece Hall when Hall was tackled into the back of Cooper Jr.'s legs. The wide receiver bent back awkwardly and limped off the field before heading into the locker room. Cooper Jr. was on the IR earlier this season with an ankle injury and was questionable coming into this week with an ankle injury, so this is a tough break for the 22-year-old.

Headline: Jared Goff completed 20-of-31 passes for 303 yards, three touchdowns, and two interceptions in the Lions’ 35-10, Week 10 win over the Patriots.
News Snippet: The Lions’ offense faced almost no resistance from New England. Goff averaged 9.8 yards per attempt and Jahmyr Gibbs ran for seven yards per carry. Goff did, however, force two throws that simply weren’t there. Both came in the second quarter, and the second pick was in the back of the end zone, costing the Lions at least three points. On the whole, it was still business as usual for one of the league’s best offenses. Goff gets a tough matchup versus the Bucs next week, but that won’t knock him out of the QB1 ranks.

Headline: Travis Kelce suffered an ankle injury in Kansas City’s Week 10 game against the Falcons and is questionable to return.
News Snippet: Already nursing an ankle issue, Kelce got rolled up at the end of a first quarter reception and hobbled gingerly to the sideline. He tried to re-enter, but ran off the field after briefly checking back in. He then headed to the locker room. We would assume veteran Kelce is genuinely questionable, and that he could get taped up/receive a pain-killing injection and return.

Headline: Panthers declared TE Ja’Tavion Sanders, RB AJ Dillon, DT TeRah Edwards, C Sam Hecht, QB Haynes King, CB Will Lee, and LB Bobby Okereke inactive for Week 10 against the Saints.
News Snippet: Sanders will be out against the Saints, meaning Tommy Tremble will get a decent number of snaps and routes. He’ll be the TE2 behind Darren Waller, coming off his biggest game of the season. The Saints this season have allowed the third highest fantasy points per target to opposing tight ends.

Headline: Colts declared QB Riley Leonard, LS Luke Rhodes, LB Jaylon Carlies, OT Jalen Travis, TE Will Mallory, and DT Jerry Tillery inactive for Week 10 against the Dolphins.
News Snippet: The Colts already declared several players out prior to Sunday’s game against the Dolphins. Leonard will be the emergency third quarterback while Rhodes (hamstring), Carlies (neck), Travis (knee), Tillery (calf) and Mallory (hamstring) are dealing with injuries.

Headline: Omar Cooper Jr. (ankle) is officially active against the Bills in Week 10.
News Snippet: That means all of Cooper Jr., Garrett Wilson, and Adonai Mitchell will be active. This is a good matchup against the Bills’ secondary in a game where the Jets figure to be trailing and needing to throw; however, it’s hard to predict which of the Jets’ wide receivers will deliver in that one. That makes Cooper Jr. a risky FLEX option. The Jets declared WR Tim Patrick, TE Jelani Woods, EDGE Nate Lynn, LB Trevin Wallace, and CB Jarvis Brownlee Jr. inactive for Week 10 against the Bills.

Headline: Tyjae Spears (knee) is active for Week 10 against the Jaguars.
News Snippet: Spears is active for the first time since Week 6. He will pick up some work on passing downs but isn’t much more than an RB4 for fantasy purposes. Inactive for the Titans are WR Carnell Tate, LB Anthony Hill Jr., LB Cody Barton, RB Nick Singleton, OT Brandon Crenshaw-Dickson, and CB Jaylon Jones, and DL Jackie Marshall.

Headline: Christian Benford (wrist) is active for Week 10 against the Jets.
News Snippet: Benford was questionable due to a wrist injury suffered in last week’s game against the Vikings. With Jordan Hancock also coming off the injured list, the Bills have a fully healthy secondary, including the addition of safety Amani Hooker. The Bills declared QB Shane Buechele, OT Jude Bowry, OL Ar’maj Reed-Adams, DL Greg Gaines, OLB Mike Danna, and S Jalon Kilgore inactive.

Headline: Chris Bell (knee) is inactive for Week 10 against the Colts.
News Snippet: Bell entered the weekend doubtful after re-aggravating his knee in practice and not practicing on Thursday or Friday. Despite the absence of Bell, no Dolphins pass-catchers get a boost with Kyle McCord at quarterback. Dolphins also declared OL Aaron Brewer, CB Marcellas Dial Jr., TE Justin Joly, WR Jared Wayne, and OL Caedan Wallace inactive for Week 10 against the Colts.

Headline: Will Anderson Jr. (ankle) is active for Houston’s Week 10 game against the Browns.
News Snippet: Anderson was questionable and did not practice on Friday, so he’s presumably gutting it out as the Texans go without Danielle Hunter (hamstring) and Azeez Al-Shaair (groin) in what looks like a must-win game. Also ruled out on Friday and Saturday were Marvin Harrison (hamstring), TE Brevin Jordan (finger/foot), C/G Keylan Rutledge (neck) and David Montgomery (groin), and they’re joined by G Wyatt Teller (back/illness) on the inactives list.

Headline: Falcons declared WR Zachariah Branch, QB Andy Dalton, LB Divine Deablo, CB Avieon Terrell WR, QB Jack Strand, CB Robert Longerbeam and OL Cameron Williams inactive for Week 10 against the Chiefs.
News Snippet: It has been a disappointing rookie season for third-rounder Branch, who seemed like he might be in line for some first-year targets. Instead he has under 100 yards receiving and is now injured. A first-year washout like this makes Branch something of a dicey long-term prospect in Dynasty leagues.

Headline: Jaguars C Robert Hainsey (consussion) is active for Week 10 against the Titans.
News Snippet: Hainsey cleared concussion protocol earlier this week and is good to go. Inactive for the Jags are S Jessie Bates III, WR CJ Williams, DT Jordan Davis, DE Wesley Williams, and DT Albert Regis.

Headline: Chris Brooks is active for the Packers’ Week 10 game against the Vikings.
News Snippet: Running backs Josh Jacobs (thumb) and Pierre Strong are both out for this one, meaning the Packers will rely on the trio of Brooks, MarShawn Lloyd, and Kaleb Johnson to handle backfield duties against a stout Vikings defense. Johnson “broke out” for 14-68-1 on the ground in last week’s win over the Patriots, but will be hard to trust this week given the multiple injuries it took for him to become fantasy relevant in Week 10. It could be best to avoid this situation altogether, especially with the Packers boasting one of the most explosive passing games in the league. The Packers declared LB Zaire Franklin, OL Donovan Jennings, OG Kevin Zeitler, and OL Sean Rhyan inactive for Week 10.

Headline: Jordan Addison (thumb) will not play in Week 10 against the Packers.
News Snippet: After injuring his thumb in Friday’s practice, Addison has officially been ruled out for Sunday’s pivotal NFC North tilt against the Packers. With Jauan Jennings (calf) and T.J. Hockenson (wrist/chest) also sidelined, Kirk Cousins will be forced to rely on Myles Price, Tai Felton, and Jeshaun and his other receivers behind Justin Jefferson. Jefferson could be in line for a big day in his first game with Cousins since 2023. The Vikings also ruled out QB Kyler Murray, QB Max Brosmer, LB Blake Cashman, and DL Tyrion Ingram-Dawkins for Sunday’s game.

Headline: Denzel Boston (toe) is active for Cleveland’s Week 10 game against the Texans.
News Snippet: He got in just one practice and was spotted in a boot at times before being dubbed questionable, but will be a reasonable WR3 play against a Texans defense missing a few pieces. Inactive for the Browns are S Ronnie Hickman (concussion), C Parker Brailsford, QB Dillon Gabriel (third quarterback), QB Taylen Green, CB Noah Ignioghene and LB Justin Jefferson.

Headline: NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo reports Baker Mayfield (leg) could miss Week 11 against the Lions.
News Snippet: Mayfield suffered a lower leg injury in Week 9 against the Bears. He played through it then, but clearly it became a bigger issue after the adrenaline wore off. The Bucs are currently on bye, giving him some extra time to recover, but it may not be enough. Mayfield’s absence would give us another round of Jalon Daniels. The UDFA rookie made three starts earlier this year. He topped out at 189 passing yards and one touchdown.

Headline: Spencer Brown (ankle) will play in Week 10 against the Jets.
News Snippet: Brown had been questionable to play after not getting in any full practices during the week. The Bills’ right tackle went through an extensive pre-game workout before he and the team declared himself good to go. The Bills will have their full offensive line healthy for this matchup against the Jets.

Headline: Bengals RG Dalton Risner (illness) is questionable for Week 10 against the Steelers.
News Snippet: Offensive tackle Myles Hinton is also questionable with an illness. It looks like something is going around the Cincy locker room.

Headline: Drake Maye (ankle) will not return in Week 10 against the Lions.
News Snippet: Aidan Hutchinson hip-drop tackled Maye for a sack early in the first quarter. Maye limped off the field and made his way to the locker room shortly after going down. He was initially listed as questionable to return but has since been downgraded to out. A dreaded high-ankle sprain appears to be on the table right now. The good news is that the Patriots get their bye next week, which will give Maye some extra time to recover. Tommy DeVito will close out Week 10 under center.

Headline: Morgan Moses (knee) returned to the Patriots’ Week 10 game against the Lions.
News Snippet: Moses limped off the field in the first quarter and immediately left for the locker room. He was briefly listed as questionable to return but managed to get back on the field in the second quarter.

Headline: Morgan Moses (knee) is questionable to return in Week 10 against the Lions.
News Snippet: Things are going from bad to worse for the Pats. Drake Maye left the game with an ankle injury in the first quarter. Moses then followed him to the locker room a few minutes later. Both are questionable to return.

Headline: Drake Maye (ankle) is questionable to return in Week 10 against the Lions.
News Snippet: Maye’s ankle rolled while he was being sacked early in the first quarter. He initially appeared ready to play through it, but Maye walked to the locker room at the start of the Pats’ next drive. The fact that Maye was able to walk off under his own power, albeit with a slight limp, is at least a good sign. Tommy DeVitto is under center for the Pats.

Headline: Aidan Hutchinson (knee) is questionable to return in Week 10 against the Patriots.
News Snippet: Hutchinson jumped in the air to celebrate a sack in the first quarter. His right knee buckled when he landed and the star pass-rusher stayed on the field for a while. He was eventually able to walk off under his own power but headed straight into the locker room. Hutchinson would be a massive loss for a Detroit defense that hasn’t played particularly well this year.

Headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Trent Williams (shoulder) is expected to play in Week 10 against the Cowboys.
News Snippet: Williams injured his shoulder during Thursday’s practice. The team then held him out of Friday’s session before listing him as questionable. It was likely a precautionary move as Williams is good to go for today’s game, which is great news for a 49ers offense that is very banged up otherwise.

Headline: Tyjae Spears (knee) is expected to play in Week 10 against the Jaguars.
News Snippet: Spears hasn’t played since Week 6 because of the knee issue. He practiced in full this week but was still listed as questionable on Friday. He should be good to go for pass-catching duties in a game that will likely see the Titans throw a lot. Spears is a low-ceiling FLEX play in PPR leagues this week.

Headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports Denzel Boston (toe) is expected to play in Week 10 against the Texans.
News Snippet: Boston will likely go through a workout in the morning to determine his status, but he appears to be on the right side of questionable for now. He was held out of the Browns’ first two practices of the week before getting in a limited session on Friday. Barring a setback ahead of kickoff, Boston is back in the WR3 mix for Week 10.

Headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Gardner Minshew suffered a torn UCL and will undergo season-ending surgery.
News Snippet: This was the expectation after Minshew severely injured his elbow in Week 9 against the Seahawks. His season is over after one incomplete start. Minshew threw for 354 yards and three scores in 2026. The surgery could sideline Minshew for over a year, meaning he may not play in 2027.

Headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Patrick Mahomes suffered a “very small sprain of his UCL” and a muscle strain in Week 9 against the Jets.
News Snippet: Mahomes’ right arm was clobbered by a Jets defender while attempting to throw a pass late in the first half of Week 9. It looked like a serious issue at first, but he managed to finish the game and didn’t even miss any practice time this week. Per Schefter, the Chiefs consulted with physicians from the Rangers and Royals, who are among the world’s best doctors when it comes to shoulder and elbow injuries. Both doctors cleared him to play.

Headline: Rhamondre Stevenson (knee) is active for Week 10 against the Lions.
News Snippet: There’ll be no Corey Kiner SZN then. I’ll tell the children. Stevenson is somewhat shockingly active after injuring his knee in Week 9. Initial reports had him missing multiple weeks. Instead, he’s good to go, though we should still expect Kiner to mix in for a few touches. Inactive for the Pats are QB Behren Morton, OG Ben Brown, OG Walter Rouse, OT Dametrious Crownover, CB Carlton Davis, and S Brenden Schooler.

Headline: Amon-Ra St. Brown (ribs) is active for Week 10 against the Patriots.
News Snippet: No surprise here. St. Brown is good to go as a mid-range WR1 for Week 10. Sione Vaki is also active. Inactive for the Lions are CB D.J. Reed, C Cade Mays, DB Keith Abney II, LB Amen Ogbongbemiga, DT Mekhi Wingo, and EDGE Ahmed Hassanein.

Headline: A.J. Brown (ankle/knee) is active for Week 10 against the Lions.
News Snippet: Rhamondre Stevenson is also active. Brown made the trip to Germany and was limited in all three practices this week. He has been dealing with knee issues for several years, and we’re sure this isn’t the last we will hear of it in 2026. Still, he has been cleared for action today, meaning fantasy managers should get him in their lineups. We’re treating him as a volatile WR2.

Headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports the Raiders planned to start Fernando Mendoza “in the next few weeks” even if Kirk Cousins had not been traded.
News Snippet: With games against the Seahawks and Broncos on tap for Mendoza’s first two starts, the Raiders may have wanted to throw Cousins to the wolves for those games before getting the No. 1 overall pick under center against Cleveland. Instead, the Vikings offered Vegas a third-round pick for Cousins and the Raiders couldn’t say no. Mendoza will make his first NFL start at home versus Seattle today. We expect him to be in the QB2 mix at some point this year, but it might take a few weeks given Vegas’s tough schedule.

Headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports the Vikings have talked to Kirk Cousins “about returning to Minnesota for the 2027 season.”
News Snippet: Rapoport notes that the Vikings told Cousins they wanted him around beyond this year before their trade for him was complete. They would go on to pay a third-round pick to reunite with their former starter. Even if Cousins is far from a superstar quarterback, head coach Kevin O’Connell is clearly sick of the weekly carousel under center. The Vikings will be legitimate Super Bowl contenders if Cousins can just play as well as he did in Vegas. A deep playoff run will all but guarantee him a spot on the roster next year.

Headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Jaelan Phillips (hamstring) is expected to play in Week 10 against the Saints.
News Snippet: Phillips hasn’t played since Week 6 because of the hamstring issue. One of Carolina’s biggest offseason additions, Phillips was off to a solid start to the year before going down. He had 2.5 sacks in five games, two of which he left early. Getting Phillips back will be a big win for the Panthers’ defense.

Headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Joey Porter Jr. (ankle) is “trending towards playing” in Week 10 against the 49ers.
News Snippet: Fellow Dallas cornerback Daron Bland is also expected to play. We don’t foresee the Cowboys putting up much of a fight against the 49ers offense, but having both corners available will at least help them slow San Francisco down a bit. Porter has appeared in four games for the Cowboys this year. He has three pass breakups and eight combined tackles.

Headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Jordan Addison (thumb) “will have his status determined closer to game time.”
News Snippet: Addison injured his thumb in practice on Friday and the team listed him as questionable for today’s game. The team elevated wide receiver Jeshaun Jones from the practice squad yesterday, casting some doubt on Addison’s availability. With Jauan Jennings also out, Tai Felton and Myles Price could be in line for larger roles today.

Headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Will Anderson (ankle) is expected to play in Week 10 against the Browns.
News Snippet: Anderson was added to the injury report on Thursday, then downgraded to a DNP on Friday. He was on the report earlier this year with the ankle injury. We suspect it flared up on him mid-week. The good news for Texans fans is that it won’t stop him from facing the Browns. With 9.5 sacks to his name through eight games, Anderson is in the midst of another elite season.

Headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Garrett Wilson cleared the NFL’s concussion protocol and will play in Week 10 against the Bills.
News Snippet: Wilson missed Week 9 because of the concussion but has cleared the league’s concussion protocol ahead of today’s game. Jets coach Aaron Glenn told reporters on Friday he expected Wilson to play, so this doesn’t come as much of a surprise. In a potential shootout with the Bills, Wilson will push for a high-end WR2 designation this week.

Headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Amon-Ra St. Brown (ribs) is expected to play in Week 10 against the Patriots.
News Snippet: St. Brown played through the rib injury last week. He remained limited in all three practices before this week’s game. He’s likely not at full strength, but there was never much risk of him missing today’s game. He remains a high-end WR1.

Headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Rhamondre Stevenson (knee) is expected to play in Week 10 against the Lions.
News Snippet: A.J. Brown is also expected to play. We will get confirmation from the team within the hour, but fantasy managers who are already rising and grinding can get Stevenson and Brown back in their lineups. Stevenson will shuffle back into the RB2 mix. We will expect to see some Corey Kiner touches to keep Stevenson fresh.

Headline: David Njoku (fibula) is questionable for Week 10 against the Ravens.
News Snippet: Njoku logged a week of limited sessions before drawing the questionable tag for Monday Night Football. He will need to be activated from injured reserve prior to Monday to play. Fantasy managers are likely better off making alternate plans considering the Chargers don’t play until Monday.

Headline: Ladd McConkey (back) is questionable for Week 10 against the Ravens.
News Snippet: McConkey heads into Monday Night Football listed as questionable after failing to practice through Friday. The veteran receiver missed Week 9 when it was revealed he had been dealing with back spasms during warmups. Fantasy managers are likely better off making alternate plans considering the Chargers play in the final game of the week.

Headline: Packers activated RB Chris Brooks and WR Skyy Moore from injured reserve.
News Snippet: Brooks returns to a backfield once again without Josh Jacobs, appearing likely to serve as the preferred passing down back while Kaleb Johnson handles early-down duties. Moore remains unlikely to be consistently involved in the offense but brings a sizable boost to the special teams unit. The top duo of Christian Watson and Matthew Golden should continue to dominate targets through the air for one of the most pass-heavy offenses in the league.

Headline: Patriots placed RB TreVeyon Henderson (illness) on injured reserve.
News Snippet: Henderson will now miss the coming four games, at minimum, after missing the previous two, with what the team is calling neurological symptoms. Whatever it is that Henderson is currently going through is clearly bigger than football. Rhamondre Stevenson is currently listed as questionable for Week 10 but is not expected to play, leaving the backfield in the hands of Corey Kiner in the immediate future. Here’s hoping for a speedy recovery for the electric running back.

Headline: Panthers activated WR Xavier Legette (knee) from injured reserve.
News Snippet: Legette will make his return to a passing offense currently dominated by Tetairoa McMillan, Jalen Coker, and tight end Darren Waller, unlikely to return a usable fantasy score in his first game since Week 2. He is not on the fantasy radar despite the plus matchup against the Saints.

Headline: Panthers downgraded Jonathon Brooks (core) to out for Week 10 against the Saints.
News Snippet: Brooks will miss his seventh consecutive game as he attempts to return from a core muscle injury. He managed a week of limited sessions before initially being listed as doubtful, ultimately ruled out. Chuba Hubbard will again serve as a legitimate workhorse in a plus matchup against the Saints and can be treated as a back-end RB1 in Week 10.

Headline: Cowboys placed RB Tyler Goodson (ankle/knee) on injured reserve.
News Snippet: It’s yet another blow to the depth of a backfield devastated by injuries this season, leaving lead back Javonte Williams again positioned well to see a workhorse role against the 49ers. The team elevated running back Israel Abanikanda in an associated move, who is likely to serve as the primary change of pace option in Week 10.

Headline: Texans ruled out David Montgomery (groin) for Week 10 against the Browns.
News Snippet: Montgomery entered the weekend listed as questionable after missing the previous three games plus the team’s Week 8 bye. Fantasy managers will have to wait another week for his return, while Woody Marks retains viable FLEX status playing as the top option alongside recent signee Emari Demercado.

Headline: Pat Freiermuth (illness) is questionable for Week 10 against the Bengals.
News Snippet: Freiermuth was added to the injury report Saturday as questionable with an illness. A mid-range TE2 when healthy, Freiermuth’s potential absence likely wouldn’t change much for Darnell Washington’s fantasy outlook. Fantasy managers counting on Freiermuth will need to be proactive about alternative options as the Steelers play the Bengals on Sunday Night Football, which airs on NBC and Peacock.

Headline: CBS Sports’ Matt Zenitz reports Omar Cooper (ankle) is expected to play in Week 10 against the Bills.
News Snippet: Cooper seemed to be trending in the right direction this week as he got in a full practice on Friday. Now he’s expected to play against the Bills, according to Zenitz. Cooper led the Jets in targets last week and will be in the WR3 mix against Buffalo this week.

Headline: CBS Sports’ Matt Zenitz reports Adonai Mitchell (knee) is expected to play in Week 10 against the Bills.
News Snippet: Mitchell remains questionable with a knee injury that put him on the injury report after getting in a full practice Friday. However concerning Mitchell’s new injury seemed, he’s expected to play, according to Zenitz. With Garrett Wilson (concussion) and Omar Cooper Jr. (ankle) also expected to play, Mitchell is a boom-or-bust dart throw at best in Week 10.

Headline: NFL Insider Jordan Schultz reports Chiefs RB Kenneth Walker (groin) is out for Week 10’s game against the Falcons.
News Snippet: Walker sat out Friday’s practice with a tight groin and was officially listed as questionable for Week 10’s game against the Falcons. Now Schultz is reporting the 26-year-old running back has been ruled out. Once that becomes official, Emmett Johnson moves into the low-end RB1 mix in a plus matchup against Atlanta.

Headline: The Ringer’s Tom Pelissero reports the Saints plan to activate Travis Etienne (hamstring) from injured reserve ahead of Week 10’s game against the Panthers.
News Snippet: Etienne practiced in full this week and now Pelissero reports he’s in line to return against the Panthers in Week 10. The 27-year-old running back deserves FLEX consideration in a plus matchup against Carolina, though he could be on a snap count in his first game in over a month.

Headline: The Ringer’s Tom Pelissero reports Packers RB Josh Jacobs (finger) underwent successful surgery on Friday.
News Snippet: Jacobs had surgery on his fractured right ring finger Friday in Los Angeles, according to Pelissero. The 28-year-old running back is expected to return in the next few weeks. In the meantime, Kaleb Johnson is the only usable Packers running back for fantasy purposes. He’s an RB3/FLEX play against the Vikings in Week 10.

Headline: New Orleans Football’s Mike Triplett reports that the Saints had Jordyn Tyson work with doctors at the University of Wisconsin to address his recurring hamstring issues.
News Snippet: Tyson has dealt with recurring hamstring injuries since October 2025, and was most recently sidelined by a hamstring strain suffered on August 13th. According to Triplett, the Saints sent Tyson to be evaluated by Dr. Heiderscheit and his team, which received a $4 million research grant from the NFL in 2021 to study hamstring issues, twice during his three-month rehab program. Dr. Heiderscheit successfully treated Packers WR Christian Watson’s recurring hamstring injuries in 2024. According to Triplett, the specialists “determined that something was a little small” in Tyson’s hamstring fascia, which allowed the Saints’ training staff to update Tyson’s exercise regimen with needed alterations. Per Tyson, the changes have allowed the tissue “to fire better.” Given Dr. Heiderscheit’s track record, Tyson’s odds of remaining healthy for the rest of the season are trending upward. He warrants WR3/FLEX treatment at this time.

Headline: Seahawks ruled out Leonard Williams (stinger) for Week 10 against the Cardinals.
News Snippet: The Seahawks’ defense should be fine without him against a Raiders offense now led by rookie QB Fernando Mendoza. The Seahawks will have LB Uchenna Nwosu (ankle) and OG Anthony Bradford (knee) on the field this week, though.

Headline: Sione Vaki (ankle) is questionable to play in Week 10 against the Patriots.
News Snippet: Vaki sat out on Wednesday and Thursday before practicing in a limited capacity on Friday. He remains a worthwhile stash as the Lions’ No. 2 running back. His backup, Jacob Saylors (neck/hamstring), is good to go.

Headline: Amon-Ra St. Brown (ribs) is questionable to play in Week 10 against the Patriots.
News Snippet: St. Brown was listed as questionable in Week 9 after practicing in a limited capacity all week. He managed to suit up on game day, posting an 8/86 receiving line. He was limited in all three practices this week and once again got hit with the questionable tag. We expect him to play. He should be treated as a WR1, as usual, assuming he is active.

Headline: Dont’e Thornton (back) is questionable to play in Week 10 against the Seahawks.
News Snippet: Thornton’s injury woes continue. The young wide receiver spent much of the year on injured reserve with a hamstring injury. He had a back injury last week, and now another back injury threatens his availability. Thornton does not need to be rostered in 12-team formats, though he provides the team with a downfield element when active.

Headline: Vega Ioane (shoulder/knee) practiced in full on Friday.
News Snippet: Ioane should have no issue playing against the Chargers on Monday night, nor should S Kyle Hamilton (hip), who has practiced in full in each of the last two days. Having Ioane on the field will be a big help for Jacoby Brissett in his first start for Baltimore.

Headline: Rashod Bateman (calf) practiced in full on Friday.
News Snippet: Bateman is firmly on track to play in the Ravens’ Monday Night Football game against the Chargers. Bateman will provide new QB Jacoby Brissett with a downfield option, but the veteran wide receiver is almost entirely reliant in ripping off one or two big plays, which has proven to be a difficult proposition for him on a weekly basis.

Headline: Keaton Mitchell (hip) was limited on Friday.
News Snippet: Mitchell is trending in the right direction for the Chargers’ Week 10 game against the Ravens. The two teams play in this week’s Monday Night Football game. Mitchell is worth stashing in 12-team leagues, but he likely lacks RB2 upside.

Headline: David Njoku (fibula) was limited on Thursday.
News Snippet: Njoku is still within his 21-day practice window and has remained limited for five straight practices. He could end up playing on Monday night, but he does not need to be rostered.

Headline: Tre’ Harris (shoulder) practiced in full on Friday.
News Snippet: Harris led the team in targets last week, but somehow managed just six yards on three catches. With Ladd McConkey (back) ailing, Harris could lead the team in targets again. He would only be a boom-bust FLEX in this case, though.

Headline: Ladd McConkey (back) did not practice on Friday.
News Snippet: This is unfortunate. McConkey is no stranger to playing through injury, but his availability for Week 10’s Monday Night Football game appears to be in jeopardy. If active, McConkey would be a WR2, but backup plans should be made at this time.

Headline: Joey Porter (ankle) is questionable to play in Week 10 against the 49ers.
News Snippet: Porter got in a limited practice on Friday. He described himself as being at 70 percent health this week. The Cowboys listed DaRon Bland (ankle) and backup S Alijah Clark (illness) as questionable, and ruled out LB Donovan Ezeiruaku (ankle) and S P.J. Locke (concussion). Cowboys LB DeMarvion Overshown (hamstring/back) will play.

Headline: Cowboys ruled out Jake Ferguson (knee/ankle) for Week 10 against the 49ers.
News Snippet: This was the expected outcome. Cowboys coach Brian Schottenheimer told reporters on Monday that Ferguson will likely be out for “multiple weeks” after suffering a knee injury. He was already dealing with an ankle injury when it happened. Ferguson does not need to be rostered in 12-team formats.

Headline: Cowboys ruled out Tyler Goodson (ankle/knee) for Week 10 against the 49ers.
News Snippet: The Cowboys will be without their No. 2 running back, removing what little threat there was to Javonte Williams’ workload. Goodson should remain stashed on 12-team benches if possible, though he could miss next week as well.

Headline: George Pickens (hamstring) is not on the Cowboys’ final injury report and will play in Week 10 against the 49ers.
News Snippet: Pickens makes his return after sitting out in Week 9. He played through the injury in Week 8, which may have been the wrong decision. The Cowboys’ No. 2 wide receiver encouragingly upgraded from limited to full participation today and can be treated as a WR2 in what should be a high-scoring game against the 49ers.

Headline: Trent Williams (shoulder) is questionable to play in Week 10 against the Cowboys.
News Snippet: Williams evidently injured his shoulder during the 49ers’ practice on Thursday, as did LB Dre Greenlaw (knee). 49ers OT Vederian Lowe would be Williams’ replacement if he cannot play. 49ers starting perimeter CBs Renardo Green (back) and Deommodore Lenoir (foot), and slot DB Upton Stout (shoulder) are also questionable.

Headline: Deebo Samuel (hamstring) is not on the 49ers’ final injury report and will play in Week 10 against the Cowboys.
News Snippet: The 49ers could end up limiting Samuel’s snaps in his first game back, but when he is on the field, he will likely be treated as the team’s No. 1 wide receiver. Samuel should be in fantasy football lineups as a WR3 with decent upside in what is expected to be a high-scoring game.

Headline: 49ers ruled out Mike Evans (Achilles) for Week 10 against the Cowboys.
News Snippet: Losing Evans for this one is a bummer. The 49ers’ and Cowboys’ offenses should facilitate a high-scoring game environment. Regardless, the 49ers are smartly prioritizing Evans’ long-term health. Whenever he returns, he is likely to be full-go. Keep him stashed on fantasy football benches.

Headline: Chris Rodriguez (hand) is not on Jacksonville’s final Week 10 injury report.
News Snippet: Rodriguez had three limited sessions ahead of this week and, should the Jaguars bludgeon the Titans, would profile to get some between-the-tackles work with Bhayshul Tuten dealing with ankle and foot injuries and not getting in much practice time. He’ll be a reasonable FLEX play against Tennessee.

Headline: Cardinals ruled out Hjalte Froholdt (concussion) for Week 10 against the Rams.
News Snippet: The Cardinals will be without Froholdt, their starting center, against a Rams team that is likely to rely on its ground game and ascending defense while navigating pass-catcher injuries. This makes life a little harder for rookie QB Carson Beck, who will make his first NFL start this week.

Headline: Chris Brooks (ankle) is questionable for Green Bay’s Week 10 game against the Vikings.
News Snippet: Brooks would have a chance to assume passing-down duties if he is activated off injured reserve. That would probably quash Pierre Strong’s value more than Marshawn Lloyd or Kaleb Johnson’s, but Brooks would probably be the favorite to see the most snaps among Green Bay’s runners if active. It would be a rough FLEX play against a good Vikings defense.

Headline: Micah Parsons (knee/illness) will not play in Green Bay’s Week 10 game against the Vikings.
News Snippet: Parsons got in limited sessions all week and seems to be in line to play in Week 11 assuming he can upgrade to full work. The Packers have slowplayed his return and have been rewarded as their defense has been able to play quite well without him.

Headline: Colby Parkinson (ribs) is not on the Rams’ final injury report for Week 10 against the Cardinals.
News Snippet: Parkinson upgraded to full participation today. Tyler Higbee (illness) was limited. Both players were cleared to play. Davis Allen (oblique) is questionable, sandwiching a Thursday absence between two limited sessions. The Rams must be smart with their skill position players’ health, while asking as much as they can from their available players.

Headline: Charles Cross (ankle) won’t play in Seattle’s Week 10 game against the Raiders.
News Snippet: He did resume practicing on Thursday, but it was a quick hook and a Friday DNP. Still, it’s an encouraging sign for his status for Week 12 — after the Week 11 bye — that he was able to get on the practice field at all.

Headline: Rashid Shaheed (knee) is not on Seattle’s final Week 10 injury report.
News Snippet: He’ll return to his boom/bust fantasy role as Seattle’s field-stretcher and punt returner after missing a few weeks due to this knee injury. Shaheed practiced in full all week and should not have any real limitations.

Headline: Drew Lock (elbow/oblique) is not on Seattle’s final Week 10 injury report.
News Snippet: Lock will step in as the starter again as Seattle takes on the Raiders, and he should profile as a reasonable superflex QB2. He was limited in all three practices this week, ceding some practice snaps to let Jalen Milroe run the show. The re-injury risk here does not quite appear to be zero.

Headline: Omar Cooper (ankle) is questionable to play in Week 10 against the Bills.
News Snippet: Cooper was limited on Wednesday and Thursday before upgrading to full participation on Friday. The team listed him as questionable for a reason, but he is likely on the right side of questionable at this time. With Adonai Mitchell (knee) suddenly ailing, Cooper could warrant WR3 treatment against the Bills.

Headline: Adonai Mitchell (knee) is questionable to play in Week 10 against the Bills.
News Snippet: Mitchell practiced in full today, but was added to the injury report with a new knee issue. This is a little concerning. The team could be trying to collect more info right now. We expect to hear more later today or at some point tomorrow. At this point, Mitchell must be viewed as firmly in the questionable column.

Headline: Chris Bell (knee) is doubtful for Miami’s Week 10 game against the Colts.
News Snippet: He did not practice Thursday or Friday after aggravating his surgically repaired knee in practice on Wednesday. The Dolphins have no reason to push Bell, so we’d be stunned if he played. Not that you were looking for reasons to lean into a Kyle McCord start, but Bell’s injury should free up targets for Malik Washington and Caleb Douglas on the FLEX line.

Headline: Garrett Wilson (concussion) is questionable to play in Week 10 against the Bills.
News Snippet: All three of the Jets’ starting wide receivers are questionable to play, though Wilson practiced in full practice and is expected to play. Wilson could handle a hefty workload if he is indeed cleared to play, as expected, and one or two of the others are limited or ruled out. Wilson is a WR2 this week.

Headline: Carson Wentz (ankle) is not on Minnesota’s final Week 10 injury report.
News Snippet: He’ll be Kirk Cousins’ QB2 on Sunday. Those of us who watched Monday’s game against the Bills are very grateful for that.

Headline: Kyler Murray (hamstring) won’t play in Minnesota’s Week 10 game against the Packers.
News Snippet: He wouldn’t have played anyway with Kirk Cousins coming over. Murray will reclaim QB2 duties when healthy, but dealing with a grade 2 strain on his hamstring, that may not be for a few weeks.

Headline: Jauan Jennings (calf) will not play in Minnesota’s Week 10 game against the Packers.
News Snippet: Jennings would have been useful additional depth to have with Jordan Addison suddenly questionable. Tai Felton will likely see more work in Week 10, and perhaps Odell Beckham Jr. will be elevated off the practice squad if Jordan Addison (thumb) also sits.

Headline: Dion Dawkins (ribs) is not on the Bills’ final injury report for Week 10 against the Jets.
News Snippet: Dawkins and LG Alec Anderson (ankle) are both good to go this weekend. Bills RT Spencer Brown (ankle) is unfortunately doubtful to play. Overall, the Bills’ offensive line health is trending in the right direction, though. Bills CB Christian Benford (wrist) is questionable.

Headline: Jordan Addison (thumb) is questionable for Minnesota’s Week 10 game against the Packers.
News Snippet: Kevin O’Connell described it as Addison getting “dinged” in practice today. Not ideal. Addison would have been in for a workload bump with T.J. Hockenson out, as it stands it looks like Kirk Cousins will just throw to Justin Jefferson 25 times like it’s 2022 again.

Headline: T.J. Hockenson (wrist/chest) will not play in Minnesota’s Week 10 game against the Packers.
News Snippet: Hockenson didn’t practice at any point this week and his status for Week 11 is likely in question as well. Gavin Bartholomew has picked up the slack this year when Hockenson has sat and will be a reasonable low-end TE2 play.

Headline: Dalton Kincaid (ankle) is not on the Bills’ final injury report and will play in Week 10 against the Jets.
News Snippet: With Kincaid’s multi-year knee injury behind him, the Bills’ tight end put together a great offseason and has proven to be a reliable player even when banged up this season. Kincaid is firmly in the TE1 ranks for this divisional showdown against the Jets in Week 10.

Headline: Danielle Hunter (hamstring) will not play in Houston’s Week 10 game against the Browns.
News Snippet: Hunter popped up on the report with this injury on Thursday as limited and wound up ruled out after a DNP on Friday. Rough scenes for the $40 million-a-year edge rusher. This will be the first game he has missed since the 2021 season. Houston’s pass rush looks tenuous against the Browns with Will Anderson Jr. also on the questionable line.

Headline: Will Anderson (ankle) is questionable for Houston’s Week 10 game against the Browns.
News Snippet: Anderson was added to the report as limited on Thursday and did not practice on Friday, throwing his status into major doubt ahead of Houston’s game in Cleveland. He has been listed with an ankle before this year, and with Danielle Hunter suddenly out, Cleveland’s pass offense could see some efficiency boosts against the Texans without their star rushers.

Headline: Marvin Harrison Jr. (hamstring) won’t play in Houston’s Week 10 game against the Browns.
News Snippet: Harrison did not practice on Thursday or Friday and it’s possible this develops into a longer-term injury. Kayshon Boutte and Xavier Hutchinson will step in as reasonable FLEX plays with Harrison’s snaps off the table. The Texans probably won’t score 40 points again, but they have struggled to move the ball on the ground and should throw plenty against the Browns.

Headline: Tank Dell (hand/shoulder) is not on Houston’s final Week 10 injury report.
News Snippet: The diminutive speedster got in back-to-back full practices and should see a reasonable workload against the Browns. He’s a low-end WR3 or high-end FLEX play at this point, with more upside possible if he’s able to repeat last week’s target share.

Headline: David Montgomery (groin) is questionable for Houston’s Week 10 game against the Browns.
News Snippet: Montgomery got in a full practice for the first time since returning from his groin injury. It’s certainly possible he’s back, but given a likely snap count in his return, it’d be hard to trust him as more than a what-the-heck FLEX.

Headline: Woody Marks (knee) is not on Houston’s final Week 10 injury report.
News Snippet: Marks was cleared after a full practice on Friday. Unfortunately, David Montgomery also got in a full practice and is questionable. Marks will retain RB2 status if Montgomery sits, but would probably go back in the FLEX bin if both are active.

Headline: Peter Skoronski (hamstring) won’t play in Tennessee’s Week 10 game against the Jaguars.
News Snippet: Not exactly what the Titans needed, losing their best offensive lineman ahead of hosting the division leaders, but it’s what they’ll get. Skoronski should be considered questionable for Week 11 as well after not practicing at any point this week following Tennessee’s Week 9 bye.

Headline: Andrei Iosivas (thumb) is doubtful to play in Week 10 against the Steelers.
News Snippet: Iosivas is still technically on injured reserve, although the team designated him to return this week. Fellow injured reserve players, CB Jalen Davis (hamstring) and OG Brian Parker (knee), are also listed as doubtful. Bengals S Kyle Dugger (quad) has been ruled out.

Headline: Tony Pollard (finger/rest) is not on Tennessee’s final Week 10 injury report.
News Snippet: A Friday tradition unlike any other. Pollard, somehow still a Titan, will suit up as an fringe RB2 against the Jaguars on Sunday.

Headline: Tyjae Spears (knee) is questionable for Tennessee’s Week 10 game against the Jaguars.
News Snippet: If Spears can play, this is theoretically the kind of blowout game script that sets him up for FLEX value via PPR scam. We wouldn’t advise chasing it, but we wouldn’t be surprised if it happened. Spears got in a full practice today, which would seem to leave him on the optimistic side of questionable.

Headline: Chiefs ruled out RT Jaylon Moore (concussion) for Week 10 against the Falcons.
