News Snippet: A fourth-round pick in 2025, Travis made four starts as a rookie and took over as the team’s starting right tackle this year. He started all nine games to open the season. Luke Tenuta will take his place in the lineup for a few weeks.

Headline: The Athletic’s Nate Atkins reports that the Rams are “hopeful” that Davante Adams (hamstring) will return for Week 13 against the Chiefs.
News Snippet: Over the next three weeks, the Rams face the Cardinals, go on bye and then face the Packers. While his potential return ahead of the fantasy football playoffs is helpful, we still have a long way to go before he returns, and even then, his status for Week 13 is still uncertain. Konata Mumpfield, Tutu Atwell and CJ Daniels appear to be in line for 11 personnel duties at this time.

Headline: Sean McVay said Puka Nacua (knee, toe) will not be placed on injured reserve for roster mechanics reasons.
News Snippet: The Rams are running out of return from IR designations. Putting Nacua on injured reserve would prevent another player from coming back later in the season, so he will simply take up a 53-man roster spot while he recovers. McVay made it clear that Nacua will still be out for a while. Nacua is expected to return at some point this year, though whether or not the Rams are still in the playoff hunt once he’s healthy could factor into the timeline.

Headline: Mike Evans (Achilles) will not practice on Wednesday.
News Snippet: The 49ers are smartly allowing Evans to fully recover from his Achilles tendinitis rather than allowing him to try to play through it. On Sunday, NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo reported that Evans was “questionable at best” for Week 10 against the Cowboys. He should probably be considered doubtful to play at this time.

Headline: Carson Beck will start for the Cardinals in Week 10 against the Rams.
News Snippet: With Jacoby Brissett in Baltimore and Gardner Minshew out because of a UCL injury, the Cardinals are already down to their third-string quarterback. It was almost a given that Beck would start at some point this year, though we imagine head coach Matt LaFleur didn’t think it would be this soon. Beck played well in his lone preseason appearance, throwing for 188 yards and a score. While he’s not much of a streaming option this week, he should be good enough to keep Trey McBride at the top of the TE1 ranks, especially with Michael Wilson done for the year.

Headline: Deebo Samuel (hamstring) will resume practicing in a limited capacity on Wednesday.
News Snippet: Samuel now has a chance to play in Week 10 against the Cowboys’ fantasy-friendly defense. The 49ers could play things cautiously and give him more time off, but an early-week return is usually a good sign. With much of the 49ers’ pass-catching corps still banged up, Samuel could return to a WR3/flex-worthy workload right away. He should be added wherever he is available. Samuel later told reporters that he feels “ready” to play on game day.

Headline: Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald said Quentin Nelson (knee) could play in Week 12 against the 49ers.
News Snippet: Macdonald also said that Nelson is “back” with the team this week. It’s unclear whether he means Nelson has simply returned to the facility to participate in team meetings, or if he actually has a chance to practice, though we assume Nelson will not practice until after the Seahawks’ Week 11 bye. Nelson underwent a procedure to remove cartilage fragments from his knee last week. If he indeed returns in Week 12, the surgery will have only cost him two games. Stay tuned.

Headline: Cardinals coach Mike LaFleur said Michael Wilson’s prognosis is “really good for the future.”
News Snippet: Wilson suffered a fracture in his neck on the fourth play of Week 9. He somehow finished the game but was placed on season-ending injured reserve after testing revealed the full extent of the injury. The good news is that this doesn’t sound like it will change the outlook of his career. He will be back next season as the Cardinals’ top wideout unless they make a big splash at his position in the offseason.

Headline: Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald said Drew Lock (elbow/oblique) will not “take every rep and throw” during Week 10 practices.
News Snippet: Lock was a limited practice participant through Week 9 practices before starting on game day. We expect that to be the case again this week. Fellow backup QB Jalen Milroe will take some first-team reps to help preserve Lock for the Seahawks’ Week 10 game against the Raiders. Given the injuries, Lock is likely just a mid-to-low QB2 despite the soft matchup.

Headline: Steelers did not open Michael Pittman’s (foot) 21-day practice window.
News Snippet: This is unfortunate, but it likely benefits Germie Bernard in the short term. Pittman told reporters that he had hoped to return following the Steelers’ Week 9 bye. The team will likely choose to ramp him up for at least one week once they open his 21-day practice window. Doing so tomorrow or Friday seems unlikely.

Headline: Steelers opened Derrick Harmon’s (foot) 21-day practice window.
News Snippet: The Steelers’ talented interior defender reportedly has a chance to play in Week 10 against the Bengals. Harmon suffered his foot injury early in Week 4 against the Browns. This season, has totaled 12 tackles, one TFL, 1.5 NFL sacks and a forced fumble. Getting him back will be a plus for the Steelers’ defense.

Headline: Carson Wentz (ankle) was limited on Wednesday.
News Snippet: The Vikings conducted a walkthrough today, so this is just an estimate. Vikings coach Kevin O’Connell said he is “hopeful” that Wentz will be available for backup duties in Week 10 against the Packers, though Max Brosmer is a possibility.

Headline: Panthers designated Jonathon Brooks (core) to return from injured reserve.
News Snippet: Brooks practiced in full, giving him a shot at suiting up this week. However, it won’t surprise us if they give him another week of practice before putting him back on the field because of his lengthy injury history. With Chuba Hubbard excelling in his workhorse role this year, Brooks will likely be stuck with change-of-pace duties once healthy. He is only worth stashing in deeper fantasy formats.

Headline: Panthers designated Xavier Leggette (knee) to return from injured reserve.
News Snippet: Legette practiced in full, so he could be back on the field as soon as Sunday. He would only return to a part-time role, so there isn’t any fantasy value to be had here. Jonathon Brooks is also practicing, meaning the Panthers’ offense could be getting reinforcements at multiple positions soon.

Headline: Patriots designated Reggie Gilliam (knee) to return from injured reserve.
News Snippet: Gilliam’s return allows the Patriots to increase their 21 and 22 personnel usage. This in turn should help out the Patriots’ run game, while also reducing target competition for the established skill position players. Gilliam is not fantasy-relevant on his own, though.

Headline: David Montgomery (groin) did not practice Wednesday.
News Snippet: It looks like Montgomery will miss another game because of the groin issue. Woody Marks has been seeing all the work in his absence. The role has yet to produce a meaningful fantasy outing. Still, fantasy managers can’t afford to fade a player seeing the bulk of the touches in an ascending offense. Marks remains a frustrating RB2 for Week 10.

Headline: Vikings GM Nolan Teasley said there is “always potential” for Kirk Cousins to remain in Minnesota beyond 2026, but acquiring him was about this season.
News Snippet: It seems that the Vikings just love to move on from quarterbacks who successfully adapt to their system. It is fair to wonder how much Cousins, 38, has left in the tank, but the fact that Teasley actually said this out loud is a little perplexing. At worst, Cousins should be able to serve as a mentor for whichever young quarterback coach Kevin O’Connell decides he wants to whisper to in 2027. Cousins is currently playing on a one-year, $11.3 million contract and could likely be retained on a one- or two-year deal at a similar value.

Headline: Cardinals activated Zach Carter’s 21-day practice window.
News Snippet: Carter has not yet played this season, but he can contribute as a run defender when healthy. The Cardinals also opened Hunter Long’s 21-day practice window, potentially bringing in blocking help for the offense.

Headline: Calvin Ridley said he does not know if he will face charges related to his altercation at the Nashville International Airport.
News Snippet: Ridley told reporters that he was trying to get his keys from the valet at the airport. They were giving him a hard time, so he took the keys out of the valet’s hands. The valet claims the altercation broke his finger. Ridley was at practice today and head coach Robert Saleh called it a “very minor miscommunication.” It doesn’t sound like the incident will keep Ridley off the field for now, though he hasn’t made much of an impact this year anyway.

Headline: Panthers designated Xavier Leggette (knee) to return from injury reserve.
News Snippet: Legette practiced in full, so he could be back on the field as soon as Sunday. He would only return to a part-time role, so there isn’t any fantasy value to be had here. Jonathon Brooks is also practicing, meaning the Panthers’ offense could be getting reinforcements at multiple positions soon.

Headline: Chiefs coach Andy Reid said the team will stick with Harrison Butker for Week 10 against the Falcons.
News Snippet: Butker has missed a field goal in every game outside of Week 1. His 63 field goal percentage is the worst mark in the league, outside of Harrison Mevis, who is not currently on a roster. Barring a sharp turnaround in Butker’s play, he’ll get benched at some point this year.

Headline: Cowboys coach Brian Schottenheimer said George Pickens (hamstring) is expected to practice Wednesday.
News Snippet: Pickens missed Week 9 with the hamstring issue. He was limited in practice throughout the week, but the team ultimately chose to hold him out for Sunday’s game. We expect one week off to be enough for the veteran wideout. Assuming things go well in practice, Pickens will be back in the WR2 ranks when the Cowboys take on the 49ers.

Headline: Patrick Mahomes (elbow) is practicing in full for Week 10 against the Falcons.
News Snippet: This comes directly from Andy Reid, though we’ll have to wait until the team’s injury report officially drops to be sure it’s actually a full session. Either way, Mahomes is playing on Sunday despite suffering an ugly elbow injury in Week 9. He told reporters it’s simply a matter of pain management for now. The Chiefs may opt to lean on their ground game against the Falcons, but even that won’t knock Mahomes out of the QB1 mix after the addition of Josh Downs.

Headline: Xavier Worthy (hamstring) practiced on Wednesday.
News Snippet: Head coach Andy Reid told reporters Worthy is “actually feeling pretty good.” Worthy went down with a hamstring injury late in the Chiefs’ win over the Jets on Sunday. The fact that he’s able to practice in any capacity today suggests he will be good to go for Week 10 against the Falcons. With Josh Downs now in the mix for targets, Worthy’s days as a relevant fantasy option appear to be over.

Headline: Ravens worked out K Harrison Mevis.
News Snippet: Riley Patterson also worked out for Baltimore. Tyler Loop is on injured reserve and Jake Moody got nabbed off their practice squad, leaving Baltimore without a kicker. One of Mevis or Patterson should get signed in the next few days.

Headline: Bengals coach Zac Taylor said Cashius Howell (wrist) is week-to-week.
News Snippet: Howell injured his wrist in Week 8 and underwent surgery shortly after the game. He was placed on injured reserve last week. Taylor declined to rule him out for the year today but didn’t offer a timeline for his return either. Howell has one tackle and three sacks this year.

Headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Josh Jacobs (finger) could miss 2-3 weeks.
News Snippet: In other words, the Packers might avoid placing Jacobs on injured reserve with his surgically-repaired finger. While he’s sidelined — including in Week 10 against the Vikings — some combination of Pierre Strong, Chris Brooks, Kaleb Johnson, and MarShawn Lloyd will handle backfield duties for the pass-heavy Packers. Johnson served as the nominal lead back in Week 9 against the Patriots, while Brooks is returning from injury and should slot in as the team’s pass-catching back. Johnson can be played as a touchdown-dependent RB3 option this week against a Minnesota defense that has shown recent vulnerabilities to the run.

Headline: Commanders head coach Dan Quinn said he expected Treylon Burks (foot) to be active for Week 10 against the Giants.
News Snippet: Burks, according to Quinn, did not practice Wednesday in preparation for Thursday night’s game against the Giants. He missed Week 9 against the Rams with a foot injury. The Commanders’ best downfield threat with Terry McLaurin sidelined, Burks profiles as a high-variance WR4 option this week. The Giants have faced deep passes at the league’s 16th highest rate this season.

Headline: Dolphins head coach Jeff Hafley said he hopes Malik Willis (groin) can return this season.
News Snippet: Hafley told reporters on Wednesday that Willis would seek second opinions on the groin injury that landed him on injured reserve. It sounds like season-ending surgery is a possibility for Willis, who would end his 2026 campaign. Through Week 9, Willis ranks 26th in passing yardage and 29th in passing touchdowns. He’s dead last in EPA per pass attempt and ranks 28th out of 38 qualifying QBs in EPA per drop back. Kyle McCord will get a chance at quarterback for the Dolphins in Week 10 against the Colts.

Headline: Colts head coach Shane Steichen said he wasn’t sure if Alec Pierce (heel) will play again this season.
News Snippet: Pierce, who signed a massive new deal with the Colts last offseason, has been on injured reserve since Week 3. The Colts have little reason to rush him back in another lost season. “We’ll see. Like I said last week, he’s still in that rehab process, and I’m not going to put a timetable on return,” Steichen said Wednesday when asked about Pierce’s availability. Steichen mentioned Deion Burks and Anthony Gould as receivers who will see more playing time after the Colts traded Josh Downs and Keenan Allen this week.

Headline: Carnell Tate (shoulder) did not practice Wednesday.
News Snippet: It’s a little concerning considering the Titans are coming off their bye week. Tate suffered the shoulder injury three weeks ago, and unless he can log a practice tomorrow or Friday, he’s likely to miss this week’s game aginst the Jaguars. His absence would make Wan’Dale Robinson viable in PPR formats, along with Chimere Dike, who led the Titans in receiving against the Bengals in Week 8.

Headline: Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said Omar Cooper, Jr. (ankle) was limited on Wednesday.
News Snippet: Cooper is dealing with an ankle issue he suffered in Week 9, but he should be OK for Week 10 against the Bills if he’s able to log a practice on Thursday and/or Friday. Cooper last week against Kansas City led the Jets in targets (11) with Garrett Wilson (concussion) sidelined. Wilson is expected back for Week 10. Cooper remains a viable flex play in a game that will likely see the Jets play from behind in a potentially pass-heavy game script. Buffalo’s defense has seen the tenth highest pass rate over expected in 2026.

Headline: Colts head coach Shane Steichen said Anthony Gould will play slot receiver after Josh Downs was traded to the Chiefs.
News Snippet: With Downs shipped out, the slot role will go to Gould, who has four receptions for 45 yards over three seasons with the Colts. Downs had accounted for 18 percent of the team’s targets and 24 percent of the team’s air yards through Week 9. The Colts use three wideout sets on 59 percent of their offensive plays, the 12th highest rate in the NFL. They rank 29th in EPA per pas attempt with three receivers on the field. Gould should be rostered in deeper formats based on route volume alone.

Headline: ESPN’s Dan Graziano reports Puka Nacua (knee, toe) will not miss the rest of the regular season.
News Snippet: Graziano said there’s an outside chance the Rams won’t put Nacua on injured reserve ahead of Week 10. Rams sources “were very adamant that Nacua’s injury isn’t season-ending and that they hope to get him back around that Week 14, Week 15 time.” With Davante Adams (hamstring) also sidelined, look for the Rams offense to be unusually run heavy in the coming weeks. That should mean more work for Kyren Williams and Blake Corum. Tyler Higbee and Colby Parkinson could see an uptick in targets too. If Terrance Ferguson (hamstring) is ever able to return to game action, he could profile as the team’s top target. Nacua had seen 44 percent of the Rams’ first-read targets this season, the highest rate in the NFL.

Headline: Cleveland.com’s Mary Kay Cabot reports Deshawn Watson (concussion) will start in Week 10 against the Texans.
News Snippet: Watson was sidelined last week against the Saints with a brain injury. He’ll back in time to face his former team as the Browns push for postseason contention in the competitive NFC North. Shedeur Sanders will revert to his backup role in Week 10 after throwing for 297 yards and two touchdowns against the Saints in an overtime loss. Watson will be a borderline fantasy option against a pass-funnel Texans defense that has allowed the third most air yards per game this season.

Headline: ESPN’s Jordan Raanan reports the Giants inquired about Bijan Robinson’s availability before the NFL’s trade deadline.
News Snippet: “They were certainly big game hunting,” Raanan said. Though the thought of the Falcons parting ways with the centerpiece of their offense sounds ridiculous, it’s clear John Harbaugh and the Giants see themselves as a postseason team that won’t be content with a playoff berth. The inquiry on Bijan speaks to the Giants’ ongoing skepticism of Cam Skattebo as a true lead back. The team has done everything they can to prevent Skattebo from taking on a big backfield workload. In Week 10 against the Commanders, with a flurry of backfield injuries and Devin Singletary coming off one of the worst running back performances in NFL history, the Giants might have no choice but to feed Skattebo, who should be started in all 12-team leagues.

Headline: Ravens released TE Nick Vannett.
News Snippet: Vannett joined the Ravens prior to the season and operated as a blocking tight end. He appeared in five games, playing 85 offensive snaps and not seeing a target in the passing games. The Ravens now part ways with Vannett on NFL trade deadline day.

Headline: Rams signed WR Xavier Smith off the 49ers’ practice squad.
News Snippet: With all the injuries at wide receiver, the Rams decide to bring back a familiar face in Xavier Smith in lieu of trading for a receiver. Smith was on the 49ers’ practice squad after the Rams waived him earlier this season. He caught 18 passes for 303 yards for the Rams last year, seeing the bulk of his opportunities as kick returner. Smith figures to operate as receiving depth with special teams utility once again.

Headline: Chig Okonkwo (hip) practiced in full on Tuesday.
News Snippet: That ought to put him firmly in the mix to play on Thursday against the Giants. Okonkwo is coming off a 6/57 game on seven targets against the Rams and figures to again be a reasonable low-end TE1 against the Giants.

Headline: Treylon Burks (foot) was limited in Tuesday’s practice.
News Snippet: It’s an upgrade from an estimated DNP on Monday. Dan Quinn has previously said that he’s optimistic Burks will play, but it’s likely that he’ll hit the questionable line tomorrow barring a full practice.

Headline: Cardinals placed QB Gardner Minshew (elbow) on injured reserve.
News Snippet: Officially he’ll miss at least four weeks, but Adam Schefter reports he’s not expected to play again this season, which essentially confirms that he tore his UCL without actually confirming it. There’s no current timeline for his return.

Headline: Eagles waived RB Jaydon Blue.
News Snippet: Not the first time this season they’ve done this, so we’re expecting a practice squad reunion here. Blue played eight offensive snaps in two weeks on the active roster and does not need to be on your fantasy team at this point.

Headline: Cowboys signed RB Kendre Miller to their practice squad.
News Snippet: Assuming all goes well, he’ll likely be elevated to be Javonte Williams’ backup this week. Dallas also has Israel Abanikanda and Jashaun Corbin as runners on the practice squad, so one of them may also get the first crack at being Williams’ backup as Tyler Goodson nurses a knee injury.

Headline: Vikings released WR Odell Beckham Jr.
News Snippet: Beckham was not targeted in his two offensive snaps yesterday. The idea of Odell Beckham being a good wideout at 34 is really fun, and the reality is that he’s played 22 offensive snaps for two teams this year. Back to the practice squad he goes.

Headline: Rams placed Jordan Whittington (back) on injured reserve.
News Snippet: Not the Rams wideout we thought we’d be placing on injured reserve today. Whittington is, nevertheless, another hit to the depth of this wideout corps. It appears to be all systems clear for Konata Mumpfield to be the No. 1 wideout who is tasked with watching Los Angeles’ running backs in Week 10.

Headline: Falcons acquired G Andrew Vorhees and a 2028 sixth-round pick from the Ravens for C Ryan Neuzil.
News Snippet: Vorhees, in the final year of his rookie contract, appears to just be in this trade as salary ballast. He struggled in a large sample in 2025 and even with injuries to the interior line in 2026 has only received 81 snaps. The Falcons may opt to turn to Corey Levin as their starter at center rather than Vorhees.

Headline: Ravens acquired C Ryan Neuzil from the Falcons for G Andrew Vorhees and a 2028 sixth-round pick.
News Snippet: Neuzil, 29, was in the final year of a two-year extension signed in the 2025 offseason. He’s played reasonably well, with a 77.4 PFF blocking grade in 2025 and a 65.1 blocking grade in 2026. The Ravens, somehow always in need of a center, find a nice piece here at the deadline.

Headline: Darnell Mooney (chest) practiced in full on Tuesday.
News Snippet: We only blurb Mooney injury reports, not Mooney game lines. There’s probably a lesson to be learned from that for fantasy managers.

Headline: Cam Skattebo (hamstring) practiced in full on Tuesday.
News Snippet: He should be good to go and handle low-end RB2 duties against the Commanders. Seemingly always at his best after a week off — which makes sense due to how physical he plays — don’t be surprised if Skattebo puts up some major fantasy points on Thursday night.

Headline: J.J. McCarthy (hip) practiced in full on Tuesday.
News Snippet: He’ll be ready to take on the Commanders on Thursday night barring a major setback. McCarthy can be penciled in as a mid-range QB2 for the game given the Commanders’ pass-funnel nature.

Headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports the Titans are holding on to Tony Pollard at the trade deadline.
News Snippet: Keeping a 29-year-old running back on the final year of his contract on your 1-7 cellar franchise is certainly a choice a team is allowed to make. We don’t know if it’s the one we’d make, but Pollard will be here to hover around RB2 value in games the Titans are pesky and RB3 value in games where the Titans offense plays as we’ve come to expect.

Headline: The Ringer’s Tom Pelissero reports Kyle McCord is set to make his NFL debut against the Colts.
News Snippet: McCord! Daniel Jones throwing to Ashton Dulin! All the stars are here in Week 10! Even in an elevated matchup, there’s little reason to believe that McCord will be more than a bottom-five superflex option this week. And this might wind up being one of his good starts, if indeed the Dolphins commit to giving him multiple cracks while Malik Willis is on injured reserve.

Headline: Dolphins placed Malik Willis (groin) on injured reserve.
News Snippet: He had clearly been laboring since the bye week and this will give Willis some time to heal. This is not regarded as a season-ending injury and Willis will be eligible to return in Week 14. In the mean time, it appears we’re all about to see how well the roster cutdown Kyle McCord trade works out for the Dolphins.

Headline: Chiefs acquired WR Josh Downs and a 2027 seventh-round pick from the Colts for a 2027 fourth-round pick and a 2027 fifth-round pick.
News Snippet: It was an obvious fit. Downs will slot in as Kansas City’s No. 2 wideout behind Rashee Rice and his fantasy stock receives a slight upgrade — though we felt like we’ve spent all year saying that and never seeing any actual returns for it — while Xavier Worthy moves back to the undesirable FLEX shadow zone. The Colts had to make this trade as Downs was a free agent at year’s end, but it has left them with a completely indecipherable wideout room. Ashton Dulin is perhaps the No. 1 target Daniel Jones has outside of Tyler Warren and Jonathan Taylor.

Headline: Panthers released WR David Moore.
News Snippet: He’ll be a candidate for a practice squad spot if he wants to stay. Moore was released to make room for the activation of Xavier Legette off injured reserve.

Headline: Broncos acquired LB Daiyan Henley from the Chargers for a 2027 fourth-round pick and a 2028 fifth-round pick.
News Snippet: The Chargers finally make a move, dealing a player who was considered a burgeoning star a few years ago away for a light deadline return. Henley had a career-worst 38.3 PFF coverage grade this year but is still a good tackler and should give the Broncos some oomph on run defense down the stretch.

Headline: The Ringer’s Tom Pelissero reports the Colts won’t trade Jonathan Taylor before today’s trade deadline.
News Snippet: Multiple teams, per Pelissero, offered a second-round pick. It sounds like Indianapolis was holding out for a first. Playing out the season in Indy, Taylor will likely retain RB1 value despite a gross situation. It should be noted that Seth McGowan had begun to cut into Taylor’s playing time a bit, but with the Colts now committed to Taylor for the short-term, it’s plausible that he’ll operate at a 70-75 percent of snaps player for the remainder of the season. McGowan retains contingency value in fantasy leagues but will not stumble into a major role barring injury.

Headline: Jordan Schultz reports the Chargers “immediately shut down all inquiries” for Justin Herbert at the trade deadline.
News Snippet: Schultz reports the Vikings called on Herbert, but the Chargers had no interest in moving on. It’s hard to understand what Herbert’s market value would have been — this has been one of the most disgusting outlier seasons for a previously good quarterback in recent memory — but the Chargers appear ready to move forward with him as their franchise quarterback.

Headline: NFL on Prime’s James Palmer reports Kyler Murray (hamstring) is dealing with a grade 2 strain, is “week to week” and is expected to miss more time.
News Snippet: In other words, Kirk Cousins could immediately slide in as the starting quarterback. As for Murray, he appears safe to drop in most formats. Call of Duty released on October 23. Not sure why that appeared in this post, but we seem to be unable to backspace it.

Headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Fernando Mendoza will take over as Raiders starter following the trade of Kirk Cousins to Minnesota.
News Snippet: We’re sure we’ll get something more official from the team once Klint Kubiak has a press conference, but this is the obvious move. The No. 1 overall pick will face a gauntlet in his first three games, starting with the defending champion Seahawks in Week 10. It’s not an immediate re-draft add situations outside of deep leagues, but Mendoza could eventually factor into the re-draft formula this season.

Headline: Vikings acquired QB Kirk Cousins from the Raiders for a 2027 third-round pick.
News Snippet: And where did that bring you? Back to me. Cousins will likely take over as Minnesota’s starting quarterback in the near future, if not immediately. When that happens, Kyler Murray will head back to the bench for a second straight season — he’s droppable in most leagues at this point. Fernando Mendoza will take over as starting quarterback for the Raiders. Mendoza is best approached cautiously at this point in fantasy leagues. Cousins’ value likely remains stagnant — Klint Kubiak was already getting quite a bit out of him — but he provides the Vikings with a better floor at quarterback than what they were getting so it’s obvious after watching Carson Wentz play last night why this is happening.

Headline: Bills acquired S Amani Hooker and a 2027 fifth-round pick from the Titans for a 2027 second-round pick.
News Snippet: It’s not Budda Baker, but Hooker has a respectable 81.0 PFF defensive grade in 495 snaps this season and has always helped as a run defender. The second-round pick is a steep price to pay and it’s quite a coup for the Titans to get that kind of return, even if they had to throw in another pick to get it done. This is all about solidifying Buffalo’s defense for a Super Bowl run for the Bills.

Headline: 49ers acquired WR Keenan Allen from the Colts for a 2027 sixth-round pick.
News Snippet: Just what the 49ers needed: To get older at the skill positions. With Christian Kirk gone, Allen figures to fill a role for the 49ers and could still be fantasy relevant depending on Mike Evans’ health. It does seem unlikely he’ll draw the same sort of targets as he had been handling for the Colts, but the targets should be more effective. The Colts signed Allen off the street in August and flipped him for something as they realized they were going nowhere, so they’ve done well for themselves here. The wideout vacuum in Indianapolis may draw players like Ashton Dulin into fantasy consideration, especially if Josh Downs also moves later today.

Headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Kirk Cousins is a “prime trade candidate” for the Vikings ahead of today’s trade deadline.
News Snippet: This would, of course, have multiple fantasy impacts. Fernando Mendoza would take over as Las Vegas’ starting quarterback if Cousins were traded, and Kyler Murray would likely take a backseat to Cousins sooner rather than later in Minnesota. We unfortunately must recommend that you stay tuned for the next couple of hours. Click the ads, too.

Headline: Free agent RB Kendre Miller is visiting the Cowboys on Tuesday.
News Snippet: With Tyler Goodson dealing with a knee injury suffered late in Sunday’s game against the Colts, Miller could find himself in a backup role behind Javonte Williams.

Headline: Cardinals signed QB Joey Aguilar off the Jaguars’ practice squad.
News Snippet: With Gardner Minshew looking at a lengthy absence, Aguilar figures to be Arizona’s No. 2 or No. 3 behind Carson Beck for the time being. Aguilar completed 17-of-20 passes for 230 yards and a touchdown in preseason action with the Jaguars after being signed as a UDFA after this year’s draft.

Headline: Falcons released K Nick Folk.
News Snippet: Folk, 42 after his birthday five days ago, had hit just 13-of-18 field-goal attempts this year after being the league’s most accurate kicker in 2023, 2024, and 2025. He’ll either resurface with a new club or have a Bluesky account in the coming days.

Headline: Falcons signed K Jake Moody off Baltimore’s practice squad.
News Snippet: They released Nick Folk in a corresponding move, leaving the Ravens holding nothing at the position currently as Tyler Loop is on injured reserve. Workouts to come for the Ravens. Moody will be a reasonable fantasy kicker provided he can do better than his 78.3 percent career field-goal conversion rate, which, of course, is not guaranteed in any way. At least he plays half his games in a dome now.

Headline: NFL insider Jordan Schultz reports the Bengals’ trade for Eagles EDGE Arnold Ebiketie has fallen through.
News Snippet: The acquisition had not been finalized, according to Schultz, who said said the nixing of the deal “is not physical or performance related.” It could be related to the Ebiketie acquisition forcing the Bengals to forfeit a 2027 3rd round compensatory draft pick that via the team’s Trey Hendrickson trade to the Ravens. In any case, the Bengals will likely head into the second half of the season with one of the league’s worst pass rushes. Only the Bills and Chiefs have fewer sacks on the season.

Headline: Bengals acquired EDGE Arnold Ebiketie from the Eagles in exchange for 2027 sixth round pick.
News Snippet: The Bengals are shoring up their defense ahead of a postseason run with Joe Burrow, Ja’Marr Chase, and Tee Higgins healthy and operating at a high level. Ebiketie, who had played 48 percent of the Eagles’ defensive snaps this season, logging zero sacks, no tackles for loss, and two QB hits, will join a Bengals defense with the NFL’s tenth highest pressure rate and tenth highest quick pressure rate on the season. Only the Bills and Chiefs have fewer sacks than the Bengals through Week 9.

Headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Dolphins DT Zach Sieler (bicep) is out for the season.
News Snippet: Sieler, who’s played well for an underperforming Miami defense, will undergo surgery on his injured bicep and remain sidelined for the remainder of the regular season. It’s a blow to the Dolphins defense, which has allowed the league’s highest EPA per play and highest offensive success rate. This could make the Dolphins more vulnerable to the run as well. Through Week 9 they have allowed the tenth most fantasy points per game to running backs, along with the 13th highest yards per carry.

Headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports the Jaguars won’t trade Brian Thomas, Jr. ahead of the NFL’s trade deadline.
News Snippet: Fowler said the Jacksonville front office has told other teams they will not part ways with Thomas before today’s 4:00 eastern trade deadline. Thomas, 24, has been an afterthought in the Jaguars offense for much of the 2026 season after a down 2025 campaign. He’s run a route on 47 percent of the team’s drop backs while accounting for 9 percent of the team’s targets and 16 percent of the team’s air yards. Thomas has seen a target on 17 percent of his pass routes, the sixth highest rate among Jags pass catchers. Stuck in Jacksonville, Thomas will have some deep league value as a big play dependent wideout.

Headline: The Athletic’s Matt Schneidman believes Kaleb Johnson could have a chance to be the Packers’ lead rusher in the coming weeks.
News Snippet: With Josh Jacobs out with a broken finger, Johnson led the Packers with 14 carries for 68 yards and a touchdown in the team’s Week 9 drubbing of the Patriots. Forty-four of those yards came on explosive rushes. Pierre Strong, meanwhile had eight carries on the day. MarShawn Lloyd was sidelined with a knee issue but could be back in the Green Bay lineup soon. Lloyd’s shocking lack of production this season could, according to Schneidman, give Johnson a real chance to seize lead back duties. Head coach Matt LaFleur after the team’s Week 9 win seemed to imply there are some pass protection concerns for Johnson. That would probably mean Chris Brooks, who’s expected to return from an ankle injury in Week 10, gets the third-down role while Jacobs is sidelined. The Packers this week take on an elite Minnesota offense that teams have run on in recent weeks.

Headline: NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo reports the Vikings could trade for a quarterback before the NFL’s trade deadline.
News Snippet: “The word going into last night was the Vikings would be in the QB market ahead of the trade deadline if Carson Wentz didn’t play well,” Garafolo said. Narrator voice: He didn’t. Wentz was an utter disaster in Monday night’s loss to the Bills, completing 8-of-25 passes for 81 yards and two interceptions in the team’s second straight loss. Wentz in Week 9 had the league’s lowest drop back EPA and lowest success rate. He also appeared to sustain an ankle injury in the second half. With Kyler Murray (hamstring) struggling mightily in Kevin O’Connell’s offense, the Vikings could make a desperation move for Kirk Cousins or Daniel Jones ahead of today’s 4:00 p.m. eastern time trade deadline. Cousins, for one, would be a marked upgrade for Justin Jefferson and the Minnesota pass catchers. The Raiders have not expressed interest in parting with Cousins, however.

Headline: Jordan Addison caught 2-of-3 targets for 28 yards in the Vikings’ Week 9 loss to the Bills.
News Snippet: Addison and the rest of the primary Minnesota pass catchers struggled through some of the worst quarterback play you will see all season, with Carson Wentz leading an offense that gained only 126 yards while failing to pick up a single first down through 55 minutes of play. Max Brosmer came on in relief of the struggling veteran late in the fourth quarter and made a few really nice throws, but the team maintains one of the worst quarterback rooms in the league. Fantasy managers are left wishing the team addresses those shortcomings ahead of Tuesday’s trade deadline to revive an anemic pass offense.

Headline: T.J. Hockenson caught 4-of-7 targets for 33 yards in the Vikings’ Week 9 loss to the Bills.
News Snippet: Hockenson struggled along with the rest of a Minnesota offense that managed only 178 yards of total offense, only 126 of which were accounted for with Carson Wentz under center. Max Brosmer came on in relief of the beleaguered veteran on the team’s final possession an nearly led the only touchdown drive of the game, ultimately coming up short on fourth down in the red zone. Hockenson and the rest of the Minnesota pass catchers are surely better off with any other quarterback than is currently on the roster, and there is the potential for the team to address the poor under-center play in the coming hours ahead of Tuesday’s 4 pm ET trade deadline. Hockenson would be a tough fantasy start against the Packers in Week 10 if the situation remains the same.

Headline: Justin Jefferson caught 3-of-11 targets for 58 yards in the Vikings’ Week 9 loss to the Bills.
News Snippet: It was a game to forget for Jefferson and the Vikings, who gained only 178 yards of total offense on just over 17 minutes in time of possession. Jefferson also failed to secure what was initially ruled on incomplete pass on a screen attempt in the first half, later overturned to a Carson Wentz fumble after being ruled a backwards pass. Furthering the pain for Jefferson’s fantasy managers is the fact that 19 of his yards came on the team’s final possession with Max Brosmer under center, leaving arguably the most talented wide receiver in the league completely bereft of a viable option at quarterback considering Wentz’s struggles. His fantasy contingency are best off saying their prayers that the team decides to address the quarterback position in the next 17 hours ahead of Tuesday’s trade deadline. Jefferson would be a middling WR2 if the position remains unchanged ahead of a Week 10 meeting with the Packers.

Headline: Aaron Jones rushed five times for 16 yards in the Vikings’ Week 9 loss to the Bills, adding five yards on one reception.
News Snippet: Jones’ six opportunities were three behind backfield-mate Jordan Mason, despite the former getting the start on paper. The Vikings were unable to move the football consistently with Carson Wentz under center, gaining just 178 yards of total offense on just over 17 minutes in time of possession, both of which heavily influenced the veteran back’s opportunities and output. Jones is far from a usable fantasy asset while sharing the workload with Mason.

Headline: Jordan Mason rushed six times for 35 yards in the Vikings’ Week 9 loss to the Bills, adding seven yards on two receptions.
News Snippet: The Vikings managed only 178 yards of total offense on just over 17 minutes in time of possession, completely incapable of moving the football with Carson Wentz under center. Those shortcomings confined Mason to only eight touches for the second consecutive week. Mason is not a starter-worthy fantasy asset until, or unless, the quarterback situation in Minnesota drastically improves ahead of Tuesday’s trade deadline.

Headline: Max Brosmer completed 6-of-7 passes for 58 yards in the Vikings’ Week 9 loss to the Bills.
News Snippet: Carson Wentz failed to convert a third down through 55 minutes of play while committing three turnovers, prompting the late switch to Brosmer on the team’s final possession. He gave the crowd something to cheer about as he completed six of seven passes, nearly matching the yardage output of Wentz on one drive. It remains to be seen if Brosmer will earn a start in the absence of Kyler Murray, although it appears more likely the team addresses the position in the coming hours ahead of Tuesday’s 4 pm ET trade deadline. Brosmer would not be on the fantasy radar if he draws a start in Week 10 against the Packers.

Headline: DJ Moore caught 3-of-5 targets for 25 yards in the Bills’ Week 9 win over the Vikings, adding 11 yards on one carry.
News Snippet: The carry was really a pass that barely went backwards on a screen in the fourth quarter, bringing his yardage total on the evening to 36. Moore has struggled through injury during his first season in Buffalo and has returned a viable fantasy outing in two of five healthy games. His next opportunity comes in Week 10 against the Jets, where he will be a middling WR3.

Headline: Dalton Kincaid caught all three targets for 28 yards in the Bills’ Week 9 win over the Vikings.
News Snippet: Kincaid was asked to block at an increased rate against a Minnesota defense that currently holds the NFL record for highest blitz rate, heavily influence both his route rate and volume. Normal TE3 Keleki Latu caught his first professional touchdown on a broken play near the end of the first half, which was the only touchdown thrown from quarterback Josh Allen. Kincaid has been one of fantasy’s biggest disappointments considering his lofty draft capital this summer, now held to four receptions or fewer in five of eight games to start the 2026 season. He’ll be a high end TE2 against the Jets in Week 10.

Headline: Dawson Knox caught 4-of-5 targets for 37 yards in the Bills’ Week 9 win over the Vikings.
News Snippet: The blocking tight end saw his snaps and routes increased against the blitz-heavy Vikings, with his 37 yards finishing second on the team behind Khalil Shakir. Even so, Knox remains unlikely to return weekly fantasy production as the blocking specialist in the run-first Buffalo offense, leaving him well outside of weekly fantasy consideration moving forward.

Headline: Khalil Shakir caught all four targets for 58 yards in the Bills’ Week 9 win over the Vikings.
News Snippet: Shakir saw his routes capped against the tenacious Minnesota defense, with the Bills increasing their 12- and 13-personnel rates to combat the most blitz-heavy defense in NFL history. He made the most of his opportunities while catching all four targets for a team-leading 58 yards. Even so, Shakir remains unlikely to return usable weekly fantasy production as a near slot-only receiver in the run-first Buffalo offense. He will be nothing more than a bye-week FLEX when the Bilsl take on the Jets in Week 10.

Headline: James Cook rushed 31 times for 107 yards and a touchdown in the Bills’ Week 9 win over the Vikings.
News Snippet: Cook struggled to 2.7 yards per carry through the first three quarters but made his mark felt in the final frame, adding his lone rushing score in the fourth quarter to bring his season total to eight. The yardage total also pushed him over 5,000 career rush yards, doing so in the same game as Josh Allen to become the first quarterback and running back duo to achieve 5,000 career rush yards in the same season. Cook has now scored in seven straight games as he continues his bid for one of the top fantasy running backs in the league. He remains an elite RB1 ahead of a Week 10 meeting with the Jets.

Headline: Josh Allen completed 21-of-31 passes for 234 yards, one touchdown, and one interception in the Bills’ 23-6, Week 9 win over the Vikings, adding 15 yards on six carries.
News Snippet: The career accolades continued to pile on for Allen, who became the fifth quarterback in NFL history to rush for 5,000 yards in his career with 15 yards on the ground against the Vikings. Furthermore, in one of the more wild statistics you will ever see, Allen and running back James Cook each surpassed 5,000 career rush yards on the same drive, becoming the first quarterback and running back duo to achieve 5,000 career rush yards in the same season. The Bills surge to 7-1 with the win and extend their lead on in the AFC East following the loss by the Patriots on Sunday. Allen and company earned every bit of it in this one, fighting through consistent pressure from the aggressive and tenacious Minnesota defense, the latter of whom kept the game within reason deep into the fourth quarter. Allen remains the top overall fantasy quarterback ahead of a Week 10 meeting with the Jets on the road.

Headline: Carson Wentz completed 8-of-25 passes for 81 yards and two interceptions in the Vikings’ 23-6, Week 9 loss to the Bills.
News Snippet: Wentz also lost a fumble as the team failed to convert a third down for the first time since 2013. The veteran backup was pulled from the game late in the fourth quarter, watching from the sideline as Max Brosmer finished it out. With Kyler Murray likely out another week or two with a hamstring injury and the trade deadline looming in less than 17 hours, the Vikings could elect to explore the trade market to address the position in what has become the most competitive division in football, with all four teams in the NFC North separated by one game or less through the first half of the season. It would be shocking to see Wentz start another game for the Vikings in 2026.

Headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Rhamondre Stevenson (knee) could miss a “short period of time.”
News Snippet: Reporting Monday, Schefter relayed that Stevenson is dealing with a knee tendon issue that could “sideline him for a short period of time.” While the report is about as vague as possible, fantasy managers will want to begin exploring alternatives for a running back that has outperformed his preseason draft capital through the first half of the season. TreVeyon Henderson remains sidelined indefinitely with what is being called an illness, which could leave Corey Kiner atop the depth chart in the backfield in the immediate future. The Patriots next play the Lions in Week 10, where Kiner would be a viable FLEX play, should Stevenson and Henderson miss. Schefter adds that the tendon issue is not expected to require surgery.

Headline: Cam Skattebo (hamstring) was listed as limited on Monday’s estimated practice report.
News Snippet: Head coach John Harbaugh said earlier Monday that Skattebo would be “full go” for Thursday night’s game against the Commanders. It’s good news for a New York football team that struggled mightily to run the football consistently with veteran journeyman Devin Singletary spearheading the backfield against the Eagles in Week 9. Skattebo appears likely to reclaim lead back duties moving forward.

Headline: Cardinals signed QB Josh Johnson from the Bengals’ practice squad.
News Snippet: In the wake of trading away Jacoby Brissett and the UCL injury to Gardner Minshew, the Cardinals spring into action to add veteran depth behind rookie third-round quarterback Carson Beck, the latter of whom is expected to start for the remainder of the season in Arizona. Beck will be thrust into action without the team’s starting left tackle and alpha wide receiver in Michael Wilson but will get much needed experience as the Cardinals decide the trajectory of their franchise in the final half of the 2026 season.

Headline: Vikings declared QB Kyler Murray, WR Jauan Jennings, S Jakobe Thomas, CB Chuck Demmings, S Theo Jackson, and DL Caleb Banks inactive for Week 9 against the Bills.
News Snippet: Both Murray and Jennings had been ruled out earlier in the week, leaving little surprise as the Vikings look to shake off their first loss of the season with an upset win over the powerhouse Bills on Monday Night Football. Carson Wentz starts under center and it remains to be seen who will fill the WR3 role, with Tai Felton and Myles Price the most likely candidates. The team also signed veteran Odell Beckham Jr. to the active roster Saturday.

Headline: Bills declared WR Skyler Bell, LT Dion Dawkins, LG Alec Anderson, DL Greg Gaines, OLB Mike Danna, and S Jalon Kilgore inactive for Week 9 against the Vikings.
News Snippet: Josh Allen will be without the starting left side of his offensive line for a game against the most aggressive defense in the league, a matchup that pits two one-loss teams on Monday Night Football. Expect a more ball-out-quick game plan from Allen and the Bills, something that could benefit Dalton Kincaid and Khalil Shakir over the short-to-intermediate levels of the field. The team could also look to deploy 12-personnel at increased rates to get Dawson Knox’s blocking abilities on the field, which would be a detriment to the route participation of Shakir.

Headline: Darnell Mooney (chest) was listed as limited on Monday’s estimated practice report.
News Snippet: A “chest” designation accompanied the practice status Monday, which would be a new injury for the veteran wide receiver. Either way, the expectation is that Mooney will be available to face the Commanders on Thursday Night Football in a short week.

Headline: J.J. McCarthy (hip) was listed as limited on Monday’s estimated practice report.
News Snippet: The official designation seems to track with the prevailing sentiment from the team, with the expectation that he’ll be able to play through the hip discomfort sustained in Week 9. Fantasy managers will want to monitor his level of participation during the remainder of the week, but it appears as if McCarthy will be out there on Thursday Night Football against the Commanders. The pass-funnel nature of the matchup and expected presence of McCarthy is a boost to the fantasy upside of Isaiah Likely and Malik Nabers.

Headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports the Cardinals fear Gardner Minshew may have suffered a torn UCL in Week 9’s loss to the Seahawks.
News Snippet: If this proves to be the case, then Minshew played the entire second half with the injury, gutting things out for the Cardinals against a top-notch Seahawks defense. Minshew will undergo more tests to confirm the severity of his injury, but it now looks as if the Cardinals will be turning things over to rookie third-round pick Carson Beck, who threw for 188 yards and one touchdown in his lone preseason game. Beck could be in for a rough few weeks, and the Cardinals’ receiving corps looks suddenly depleted with Marvin Harrison Jr. now on the Texans and Michael Wilson (neck) and Kendrick Bourne (leg) both done for the season.

Headline: Chig Okonkwo (hip) was listed as limited on Monday’s estimated injury report.
News Snippet: This is a new injury for Okonkwo, who caught a 16-yard pass on the final play of Sunday’s loss to the Rams as the Commanders were looking to tie the game. Okonkwo has gone for 57 or more yards in three of his last four games and would be on the streaming radar as a boom-or-bust TE2 on Thursday against the Giants if he can play.

Headline: Commanders listed Treylon Burks (foot) as DNP on Monday’s estimated injury report.
News Snippet: Hours after head coach Dan Quinn said he was “optimistic” that Burks would play in Week 10 against the Giants, the Commanders listed him as an estimated DNP for Monday. While they didn’t formally practice, the fact that the team is saying he wouldn’t have gotten on the field today isn’t an encouraging sign for a player who missed all of last week’s practices as well. The good news is there are still more practices to go, meaning Burks could still be upgraded before Thursday night’s game. We’ll see if his status changes on Tuesday when the Commanders take the practice field for the first time on the short week.

Headline: Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer said Jake Ferguson (knee) will likely be out “multiple weeks” after going down in Week 9 against the Colts.
News Snippet: Ferguson exited Sunday’s game against the Colts after taking a nasty hit to his knee. While he was able to walk off under his own power and was later ruled “questionable” to return, the 27-year-old vet never got back into the game. Ferguson has caught just 19 passes for 136 yards and four touchdowns this season, with his best game coming in Week 2 (4-43-2) against the Commanders. Brevyn Spann-Ford, a 2024 UDFA, will likely take over in Ferguson’s absence but shouldn’t be trusted as anything more than a boom-or-bust TE2 at this point.

Headline: Rams head coach Sean McVay said Puka Nacua (knee/turf toe) is likely headed to injured reserve.
News Snippet: An MRI on Monday revealed a sprained MCL and PCL for Nacua, who also suffered a turf toe injury on the Rams’ final offensive play in Sunday’s win over the Commanders. Nacua caught 14 passes for 150 yards and a touchdown in the win, drawing a target on 44.2 percent of Stafford’s pass attempts. It goes without saying that this creates a massive problem for a Rams passing game that has failed to find a serviceable WR2 sans Davante Adams (hamstring). Now, McVay and company will be faced with a new challenge as they try to replace Nacua with the likes of Tutu Atwell, Jordan Whittington, Konata Mumpfield, or a player not yet on the roster. Long believed to be buyers ahead of Tuesday’s trade deadline, it seems like a foregone conclusion that GM Les Snead will do what he can to acquire a playmaker for Matthew Stafford with whatever draft picks he still has at his disposal. The Rams currently only hold one pick in the first three rounds of the 2027 NFL Draft but still hold their first-round picks in 2028 and 2029, per Spotrac.com.

Headline: Eagles traded DT Jordan Davis to the Jaguars in exchange for a 2027 first-round pick and a 2029 second-round pick.
News Snippet: While the rest of the league waits to make moves ahead of Tuesday’s NFL trade deadline, the Jaguars have spent Monday wheeling and dealing to improve the defensive side of the ball. Davis is the latest to join the Jaguars, who also acquired S Jessie Bates and DT Davon Godchaux in hopes of shoring up their top-10 defense. Davis signed a three-year, $78 million contract extension with the Eagles earlier this offseason and has been a staple along their defensive line since being drafted 13th overall by them in 2022. Davis has totaled 31 tackles, 1.5 sacks, and two TFLs this season and posted a career-high 4.5 sacks in 2025.

Headline: Cardinals signed QB Joey Aguilar off the Jaguars’ practice squad.
News Snippet: With Gardner Minshew looking at a lengthy absence, Aguilar figures to be Arizona’s No. 2 behind Carson Beck for the time being. Aguilar completed 17-of-20 passes for 230 yards and a touchdown in preseason action with the Jaguars after being signed as a UDFA after this year’s draft.

Headline: The NFL reinstated 49ers WR Brandon Aiyuk from the reserve/left squad list.
News Snippet: According to The Ringer’s Tom Pelissero, the NFL has granted the 49ers a two-week roster exemption for Aiyuk as the two sides continue to negotiate his impending release. The 49ers will have until November 23rd to make a roster move, but once released, Aiyuk will be free to sign with any team. The 28-year-old receiver last played in 2024 and hasn’t taken a snap since tearing his ACL in Week 7 of that season. While there is a chance Aiyuk could suit up for a new team at some point this season, fantasy managers hoping to stash him shouldn’t expect anything meaningful until the fantasy playoffs at the earliest, as it could take him several weeks to find a new team and get up to speed with the season more than halfway over.

Headline: Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur said Gardner Minshew (elbow) could miss Week 10’s game against the Rams.
News Snippet: Minshew took a hard hit to his right elbow/arm in Sunday’s loss to the Seahawks and is now undergoing tests to determine the severity of his injury. He managed to play through the game, but if he is unable to go in Week 10 against the Rams, rookie Carson Beck would be in line to make his first career start. Minshew threw for 166 scoreless yards against a stout Seahawks defense, but led a comeback victory in just one half of play against the Cowboys the previous week. With recent reports of Michael Wilson (neck) being lost for the season, both Minshew and Beck would be best left on waivers this week.

Headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Cardinals WR Michael Wilson suffered a neck injury in Week 9’s loss to the Seahawks, ending his season.
News Snippet: It’s a tough and unexpected loss for the Cardinals, and Wilson, who was not reported to have suffered any injury after the game. Wilson was on track for another solid season after breaking out for 76-1,006-7 last season. He was averaging a solid 9.8 targets per game this season, and never saw fewer than seven targets in any game. Wilson signed a three-year, $75 million contract extension earlier this offseason and will hopefully recover in time to be back for the start of training camp next season. Now without the top three receivers they opened the season with, the Cardinals will likely lean on the trio of Harrison Wallace III, Reggie Virgil, and Simi Fehoko for the remainder of the season.

Headline: Packers head coach Matt LaFleur confirmed Josh Jacobs will undergo surgery on his fractured finger and didn’t rule out a stint on injured reserve.
News Snippet: LaFleur confirmed previous reports that Jacobs will undergo surgery, but it sounds like he could be at risk of missing more than the three-week “maximum” that was reported. LaFleur not only said a stint on injured reserve was possible, but also noted that Jacobs playing through the injury was never an option, saying he “had no grip strength.” We don’t yet know when Jacobs will undergo his surgery, but LaFleur did confirm that it will be some time this week. With Jacobs now sidelined for the foreseeable future, Green Bay will look to MarShawn Lloyd, Pierre Strong, and Kaleb Johnson to lead the backfield heading into Week 10 against the Vikings.

Headline: Saints head coach Kellen Moore said C Erik McCoy is expected to miss some time with a bicep injury
News Snippet: McCoy missed 10 games last season due to a torn biceps. It doesn’t sound like his injury is nearly as severe this time around, as Moore said he believes McCoy will avoid surgery. That said, it sounds like the veteran center could be headed for injured reserve with hopes he will return at some point in the season. McCoy has started all eight games he has appeared in this season, earning a PFF grade of 73.2 while allowing just five pressures on 352 pass-blocking downs. He was replaced by Will Sherman in Week 9’s win over the Browns, with Sherman being the favorite to take over in the weeks ahead while McCoy is sidelined.

Headline: Ravens head coach Jesse Minter said he expects Jacoby Brissett to start in Week 10 against the Chargers.
News Snippet: The Ravens wasted little time in trading for Brissett after he lost his starting job with the Cardinals. The 33-year-old journeyman is familiar with Ravens QB coach Israel Woolfork and was acquired in part because the team believed he could quickly become the starter. Brissett threw for 1,719 yards, 10 touchdowns, and seven interceptions in his eight games with the Cardinals this season, and will now look to save the Ravens’ season after they fell to 4-5 last week. With Lamar Jackson (finger) hoping to come back in the next six to nine weeks, if Baltimore can string together a few wins, it’s possible he will be back in time for the playoffs should they make the postseason. Brissett being under center should also provide some stability to Zay Flowers’ and Derrick Henry’s fantasy stocks after a rough few weeks sans Lamar.

Headline: Cowboys executive vice president Stephen Jones said RB Tyler Goodson (knee) is expected to miss some time.
News Snippet: Goodson has emerged as the Cowboys’ RB2 this season, and rushed 12 times for 77 yards in Week 9’s win over the Colts. He played through the knee injury he suffered in the second quarter. The fact that he played through the injury suggests this isn’t anything too serious, but it’s not uncommon to see players be sidelined in the following weeks once the adrenaline has worn off and the game is over. We’ll likely get a clearer timeline for his return in the coming days, but for now, it looks like Israel Abanikanda and/or Jashaun Corbin will be promoted from the practice squad, with Javonte Williams being the only healthy back on Dallas’ roster.

Headline: Speaking Monday, Browns head coach Todd Monken declined to name a starting QB for Week 10’s game against the Texans.
News Snippet: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reported earlier in the day that Deshaun Watson was expected to return as the starter, but Monken didn’t rush to name a starter when questioned on Monday. Monken praised Shedeur Sanders for his performance in Sunday’s start against the Saints, but said he hasn’t really “thought through” who will start in Week 10 against the Texans. It’s hard to imagine Monken handing the job over to Sanders after a start that was mostly forgettable until the final five minutes of regulation, even if Watson hasn’t been overly impressive this season. We would still expect Watson to get the nod against Houston, but Sanders’ late-game performance won’t do anything to quiet those looking/hoping for a change.

Headline: Jets traded S Andre Cisco to the Lions in exchange for a 2028 sixth-round pick.
News Snippet: Cisco has started four of the nine games he has appeared in for the Jets this season, racking up 23 tackles, one sack, and one pass breakup while also forcing a fumble. The sixth-year safety has 59 games of starting experience and should provide some help on the back end to a secondary that has allowed the most passing yards this season. He has graded out well as a run stopper in each of his last two seasons, per PFF, and can also line up in the slot when needed.

Headline: Jaguars acquired DT Davon Godchaux from the Saints in exchange for a 2028 sixth-round pick.
News Snippet: Godchaux becomes the second defensive player the Jaguars have added ahead of the deadline. Early Monday morning, they went out and acquired safety Jessie Bates from the Falcons to improve their secondary, and now they’ve added Godchaux to bolster a defensive line that has been dealt a few injuries in recent weeks. Godchaux, like Bates, is also on an expiring contract, but should provide a small upgrade to what is already a top-10 defense. The 31-year-old lineman has totaled 15 tackles and one TFL this season while appearing on 163 snaps, with most of his contributions coming in run defense.

Headline: Chiefs head coach Andy Reid said Patrick Mahomes (elbow) is considered “day-to-day.”
News Snippet: This news comes less than 24 hours after NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reported that an MRI “did not reveal a major injury” to Mahomes, who was able to finish out the game in Sunday’s win over the Jets. Reid said Mahomes is dealing with some soreness that he will have to rehab a bit, but it doesn’t sound like he’s at risk of missing any time. Mahomes threw for 242 yards and two touchdowns against the Jets and will be on the QB1 radar next week against the Falcons.

Headline: Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald said the team expects Drew Lock (oblique) to start in Week 10 against the Raiders.
News Snippet: Speaking on Monday, Macdonald said that tests on Lock’s oblique injury were “good” and that they believe his injury is something the team can manage. Lock has been solid in three games for the Seahawks this season, throwing for 597-5-0 while completing 71.1 percent of his passes. He draws a favorable Week 10 matchup against the Raiders and could be on the radar as a mid to low-end QB2 that may have some stream appeal in 2QB/Superflex leagues.

Headline: Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald said Sam Darnold (quad) will not play in Week 10 against the Raiders.
News Snippet: Macdonald said Darnold will need at least one more week to recover from the quad injury that sidelined him in Week 9. While Drew Lock (oblique) is dealing with his own injury, Macdonald said he believes the team can manage it and expects him to start next week against the Raiders. The Seahawks will have their bye in Week 11, so hopefully three straight weeks off will give him enough time to recover before Week 12’s game against the 49ers.

Headline: Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel said the team plans to bring A.J. Brown (ankle/knee) to Germany ahead of Week 10’s game against the Lions.
News Snippet: This doesn’t mean Brown will suit up against the Lions, but it is an indicator that the team thinks he has a chance to play if he can have a good week of practice. Brown has missed the Patriots’ last two games after a knee injury flared up following Week 7’s game against the Bears. He did not get on the practice field at all last week, so even a few limited sessions would be an improvement for the 29-year-old receiver. In three games this season, Brown has caught just 9-of-20 targets for 101 scoreless yards. That said, if he’s healthy enough to play in Week 10, he could be primed for a breakout against a lowly Lions secondary.

Headline: Giants head coach John Harbaugh said Cam Skattebo (hamstring) will be “full go” in Week 10 against the Commanders.
News Snippet: Harbaugh said Skattebo was “very close” to playing in Week 9 against the Eagles, but they opted to sideline him, focusing on the second game they would play four days later. With the Giants set to face the Commanders on Thursday, Skattebo should be well rested and ready to play in his first game since Week 7, when he first suffered his injury. Skattebo totaled 71 scoreless yards on 15 touches in Week 5 against the Commanders and will be in the RB2 mix upon returning this week.

Headline: NFL insider Jordan Schultz reports the Panthers “have received calls” on DT Derrick Brown’s availability via trade.
News Snippet: The Panthers have said that they are “not actively looking to move Brown,” but Sports Illustrated’s Albert Breer reported last week that they have considered it. One of the premier DTs in the league, Brown could fetch a decent pick haul if the Panthers were willing to move him. With the NFL trade deadline set to pass on Tuesday, we will soon know the fate of several players who are rumored to be on the move, but it sounds like it will take a lot for the Panthers to give up Brown.

Headline: James Cook rushed 31 times for 107 yards and a touchdown in the Bills’ Week 9 win over the Vikings.
News Snippet: Cook struggled to 2.7 yards per carry through the first three quarters but made his mark felt in the final frame, adding his his lone rushing score in the fourth quarter to bring his season total to eight. The yardage total also pushed him over 5,000 career rush yards, doing so in the same game as Josh Allen to become the first quarterback and running back duo to achieve 5,000 career rush yards in the same season. Cook has now scored in seven straight games as he continues his bid for one of the top fantasy running backs in the league. He remains an elite RB1 ahead of a Week 10 meeting with the Jets.

Headline: Ravens head coach Jesse Minter said Kyle Hamilton “looks fairly good” after suffering a hip injury in Week 9’s loss to the Jaguars.
News Snippet: Hamilton exited Thursday’s game and did not return to the field. Despite the scare, it doesn’t sound like Hamilton is at risk of missing much, if any, time. The two-time All-Pro has totaled 60 tackles, nine TFLs, and one interception this season while also breaking up five passes.

Headline: CBS Sports’ Matt Zenitz reports Josh Jacobs will undergo surgery on his fractured finger and “is expected to miss a maximum of three weeks.”
News Snippet: Less than 24 hours after it was reported that the team would see if Jacobs could play through his fractured finger, they have now opted for surgery. The decision to say Jacobs could be out “a maximum of three weeks” suggests he will avoid the injured reserve and that this will be more of a week-to-week thing, and that he could return before the end of the month. Jacobs has totaled 148 yards from scrimmage and three touchdowns on 47 touches since returning from the Commissioner’s Exempt list. Now, the Packers will likely take a bit of a committee approach in the weeks ahead and could lean more on Kaleb Johnson, who was solid against the Patriots (14-68-1), with Jacobs and MarShawn Lloyd (knee) both sidelined. That said, all Packers running backs will be hard to trust as anything more than desperation dart throws in Week 10 when they take on a stout Vikings defense.

Headline: Buccaneers head coach Todd Bowles said Bucky Irving’s touches could decrease in the second half of the season to preserve his health.
News Snippet: As Bucs beat writer Greg Auman points out, Irving is on pace for 315 carries this season, which would have been the second most in the league last year. Irving has not missed a game yet this season, but after injuries limited him to 10 games in 2025, it’s not surprising to learn Bowles may want to dial things back a bit. The efficient play of Kenneth Gainwell in recent weeks has also earned him an expanded look, and it should instill a bit of confidence in OC Zac Robinson when asking him to spell Irving in certain situations. With the Bucs now entering their bye week, we will get our first look at how the team plans to deploy its backfield in Week 11 when they visit the Lions.

Headline: Commanders head coach Dan Quinn said he is “optimistic” that Treylon Burks (foot) will play in Week 10 against the Giants.
News Snippet: Burks sat out in Sunday’s loss to the Rams due to a foot injury that kept him off the practice field all week. Quinn’s optimism suggests he will at least be listed as limited on Monday’s estimated practice report and will get on the field in some capacity on Tuesday and Wednesday. Burks has been a solid downfield threat for the Commanders this year, catching 12 passes for 233 yards and two touchdowns. Even if he is active, fantasy managers can avoid him outside of deeper leagues, where he could be a viable desperation play as a WR4. In addition to Burks, Quinn also said he was hopeful CB Amik Robertson (ankle) would be ready to play on Thursday against the Giants.

Headline: NFL insider Jordan Schultz reports the Panthers “have received calls” on DT Derrick Brown’s availability via trade.
News Snippet: The Panthers have said that they are “not actively looking to move Brown,” but it Sports Illustrated’s Albert Breer reported last week that they have considered it. One of the premier DTs in the league, Brown could fetch a decent pick haul if the Panthers were willing to move him. With the NFL trade deadline set to pass on Tuesday, we will soon know the fate of several players who are rumored to be on the move, but it sounds like it will take a lot for the Panthers to give up Brown.

Headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports the Browns “plan to start Deshaun Watson in Week 10 vs. the Texans.”
News Snippet: This shouldn’t surprise anyone after Shedeur Sanders failed to make the most of his spot start in Week 9 against the Saints. Sanders and the Browns’ offense stalled through the first three quarters of Sunday’s game before a late 64-yard touchdown pass to KC Concepcion gave the Browns their first touchdown of the day. An impressive catch-and-run score by Harold Fannin in overtime gave Sanders his second touchdown pass on the day, but the 39-yard score came on a pass, in which Fannin generated 37 yards after the catch. Watson has struggled mightily at times this season, but Sanders didn’t do enough to unseat him in what was a plus matchup against a bad defense. Now out of concussion protocol, Watson will suit up in a “revenge game” against his former team next week, where he will profile as a low-end QB2.

Headline: Giants head coach John Harbaugh said J.J. McCarthy (hip) looks “like he’s going to play” in Week 10 against the Commanders.
News Snippet: Harbaugh said McCarthy is “doing well” after briefly being knocked out of Sunday’s game against the Eagles with a hip injury. McCarthy was in visible pain on the sideline at times, but was able to finish the game. We’ll see how things shape up over the week as the Giants prepare for a short turnaround ahead of Thursday night’s game against the Commanders. If he’s healthy enough, McCarthy will get the start against a Commanders defense that has struggled mightily at times against the pass this season.

Headline: Speaking after Week 9’s win over the Commanders, Rams head coach Sean McVay said Terrance Ferguson (hamstring) will likely be out a “couple [of] weeks.”
News Snippet: Ferguson was set to return in Week 9 against the Commanders prior to suffering a pulled hamstring. According to McVay, the second-year tight end was going to be a “big part” of the Rams’ offensive game plan against the Commanders, which should be good news to fantasy managers still holding out hope for a return. Based on McVay’s comments, we can safely assume Ferguson won’t be playing in Week 10 against the Cardinals, and then the Rams head into their bye. If all goes well in his recovery, it’s possible he could return on a short week in Week 12 to play against the Packers, but we likely won’t have more clarity on that until after their bye. For now, Ferguson remains a worthwhile stash in leagues where you can afford to do so, but it’s hard to say with any confidence when we should expect him to be back on the field.

Headline: Titans head coach Robert Saleh said Calvin Ridley was involved in an “unfortunate” incident at Nashville airport.
News Snippet: Saleh didn’t get into the details of the matter, instead opting to say it was a “very minor miscommunication” that is “now in the hands of law enforcement.” Ridley, 31, has caught 6-of-12 targets for 91 scoreless yards this season and could find himself on the move ahead of Tuesday’s trade deadline. That said, he’s far from the difference-making player he was early in his career and is fourth among Titans receivers in routes run (124) this season.

Headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Jets DE Will McDonald has requested a trade.
News Snippet: McDonald has been lightly used this season by the Jets. The former first-rounder has appeared in all nine games this season, totaling three sacks and 15 tackles while appearing on just 278 defensive snaps, per PFF. According to Rapoport, the Jets have not engaged in trade talks for McDonald despite receiving calls, and “they have no plans to.” With a 2-7 record, the Jets should be sellers, but have maintained for over a week that they would prefer not to move many players, if any.

Headline: Falcons traded S Jessie Bates to the Jaguars in exchange for a 2027 second-round pick.
News Snippet: The Jaguars also sent a 2028 fifth-round pick to the Falcons in exchange for Bates, who is in the final year of his contract. Bates provides an immediate upgrade to a defensive unit that already ranks top-10 in points and yards allowed per game but has been more susceptible to being hurt through the air. Bates is a three-time Second-Team All-Pro and among the top safeties in the league. It stands to reason that the Jaguars will look to extend him at some point next offseason, but for now, he will join a 6-2 team that is clearly willing to go all in on what could be a deep run in the postseason.

Headline: Chris Godwin caught 2-of-3 targets for 16 yards in the Buccaneers’ Week 9 loss to the Bears.
News Snippet: The only positive to take from this is every Tampa Bay receiver who caught a pass clobbered their production from the week before. Godwin did have a 12-yard rush, but it’s another clunker for the wideout in a year where Godwin has yet to reach 50 yards. It’s a mistake to bet that mark will be reached in Week 11 against the Lions after their bye.

Headline: Cade Otton caught 4-of-6 targets for 25 yards in the Buccaneers’ Week 9 loss to the Bears.
News Snippet: Otton was targeted a couple of times in the end zone, but Baker Mayfield wasn’t able to connect with the tight end on either attempt. The 25 yards are his most since Week 5, but it’s still a middling — at best — effort for the 27-year-old. Fantasy managers should look elsewhere in Week 11 against the Lions after Tampa Bay’s bye.

Headline: Emeka Egbuka caught 3-of-5 targets for 38 yards in the Buccaneers’ Week 9 loss to the Bears.
News Snippet: It was Egbuka’s first game since Week 6 because of his foot injury, and it was pretty similar to his previous efforts in 2026. He was able to get lose for a 21-yard catch from the arm of Baker Mayfield, but once again, he was unable to eclipse 50 yards; a mark he hasn’t bested since Week 3. Egbuka is a high-floor, low-ceiling WR3 going forward, and the next chance will come after a bye in Week 11 against the Lions.

Headline: Tez Johnson caught 2-of-5 targets for 76 yards in the Buccaneers’ Week 9 loss to the Bears.
News Snippet: Johnson’s 58-yard connection with Baker Mayfield set up a rushing score from Bucky Irving. He also had two big drops on third down that would have kept drives going for the Bucs, and on the first he was seen taking out his frustration on his helmet. Johnson ended up leading the Bucs in receiving yards and tied for the lead in targets, but that’s not quite the compliment it should be. Johnson and Tampa Bay get a bye before a showdown with the Lions in Week 11.

Headline: Kalif Raymond caught 4-of-7 targets for 32 yards in the Bears’ Week 9 win over the Buccaneers.
News Snippet: Raymond had a quiet day, but made a huge 13-yard catch on the final drive that ended with a Cairo Santos’ game-winning field goal. Luther Burden exited the game with a head injury late, and if Burden can’t go in Week 11 after the bye, Raymond will be an intriguing dart throw for that contest. If Burden can go, he’s tough to trust in redraft formats.

Headline: Rome Odunze caught 4-of-7 targets for 60 yards and a touchdown in the Bears’ Week 9 win over the Buccaneers.
News Snippet: Odunze couldn’t quite haul in a touchdown throw from Caleb Williams on the first drive of the game, but on the next play, he was able to reach the end zone for his first touchdown of the 2026 season. He could have had another, but a perfect throw from Williams bounced off his hands with nothing but green grass in front of him. Still, it’s another competent game for the former first-round pick, and he’s reached 60 yards in each of his last three contests. Odunze belongs in the WR3 range for Week 11 against the Saints after a Week 10 bye.

Headline: D’Andre Swift rushed 12 times for 31 yards in the Bears’ Week 9 win over the Buccaneers.
News Snippet: Swift didn’t catch his lone target in a bust of a contest for the veteran tailback. He had a long gain of just six yards, and was nearly outrun by Salvon Ahmed who finished with 25 yards on the ground. Yes, that Salvon Ahmed.
